mwg:cross-document-transitions.story: Page changes on multi-page sites have always been a full-page flash. Now one declaration on each page gives a transition, and unsupported browsers navigate as usual with no fallback to write.
mwg:cross-document-transitions.unlock: Animated page changes used to require an SPA → statically generated sites (docs, portfolios, journals) get transitions from two lines of CSS. Firefox falls back to normal navigation
mwg:cross-document-transitions.support: View transitions: Newly (2025-10-14); Cross-document view transitions: Limited availability, Supported by: Chrome 126, Edge 126, Safari 18.2; Unsupported in: Firefox

mwg:cross-document-transitions:2.title: Use transition types so "back" and "forward" move in opposite directions
mwg:cross-document-transitions:2.action: When a page always uses one direction, write `types: previous` in `@view-transition`; when it depends on the origin, compute a type from `navigation.activation` in `pagereveal` and call `e.viewTransition.types.add()`, then style each with `:active-view-transition-type()`
mwg:cross-document-transitions:2.blocker: With one effect for every navigation, going back to the home page slides in from the right just like going forward, which makes no spatial sense (quote: "When navigating back to the home page, it wouldn't make sense to have the same effect.")
mwg:cross-document-transitions:2.outcome: Forward and back each get a directional transition; without the Navigation API you need another way to pick the type or a default; Firefox doesn't support cross-document transitions (official claim)
mwg:cross-document-transitions:2.story: As soon as a slide transition works you notice going back also "slides forward". Types let the same set of pages choose an animation by how they relate.
mwg:cross-document-transitions:2.unlock: Transitions on multi-page sites couldn't tell direction → step-by-step tutorials, previous/next in galleries, and article series can each slide the right way. Firefox falls back to normal navigation
mwg:cross-document-transitions:2.support: Cross-document view transitions: Limited; Navigation API: Newly (2026-01-13)

mwg:custom-button-actions.title: Declare what a button does to which element with `command="--custom"`
mwg:custom-button-actions.action: Give buttons `commandfor="target-id"` and a custom command starting with `--` such as `command="--spin"`; listen for `command` on the target, look up `event.command` in a registry, and use `event.source` to update the button's `aria-pressed` / `aria-expanded`
mwg:custom-button-actions.blocker: The guide only says it reduces manual event listeners and decouples UI from implementation, without saying when hand-wired listeners go wrong (quote: "This approach reduces the need for manual event listeners and decouples the UI from implementation details.")
mwg:custom-button-actions.outcome: The button-to-target relationship lives in HTML and one listener handles every command; Invoker commands are Newly, older browsers get the same event from a polyfill, but the polyfill doesn't manage ARIA states (official claim)
mwg:custom-button-actions.story: Each button used to get its own `addEventListener` and find its target, so renaming an id meant editing JS. Now buttons just declare "to whom, what", and behaviour lives in one command table on the target.
mwg:custom-button-actions.unlock: A set of controls used to need JS wired to each button → player, canvas editor, and kanban card actions can be written in HTML as `--play`, `--zoom-in`, `--archive`, and server-rendered pages ship working buttons
mwg:custom-button-actions.support: Invoker commands: Newly (2025-12-12), Supported by: Chrome 135, Edge 135, Firefox 144, Safari 26.2

mwg:custom-button-actions:2.title: `command` doesn't bubble: attach the listener to the target
mwg:custom-button-actions:2.action: Attach the `command` listener directly to the target; when targets vary, listen on an ancestor with `{ capture: true }`; when the target may be in a shadow root, use `event.composedPath()[0]`
mwg:custom-button-actions:2.blocker: The `command` event doesn't bubble, so a delegated listener on an ancestor never receives it (quote: "The `command` event does not bubble.")
mwg:custom-button-actions:2.outcome: Listening on the target or in the capture phase receives the command (official claim)
mwg:custom-button-actions:2.story: Anyone used to delegating events on `document` writes their first `command` handler and finds nothing happens.

mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control.title: Open and close dialogs from HTML with `command="show-modal"` and `toggle-popover`
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control.action: `<button commandfor="id" command="show-modal">` opens a modal `<dialog>` and `command="close"` closes it; popovers use `toggle-popover`, or separate `show-popover` / `hide-popover`
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control.blocker: The guide only says it removes brittle boilerplate and makes interactions work as soon as HTML is parsed, without saying when hand-written listeners go wrong (quote: "removes brittle boilerplate code, ensures interactions are functional immediately upon HTML parsing")
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control.outcome: The browser handles open/close state, focus management, and `aria-expanded`; Invoker commands are Newly, older browsers need a conditionally loaded polyfill that doesn't handle `aria-expanded` like native (official claim)
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control.story: Opening a confirm dialog used to take at least a snippet of `showModal()` JS. Now the button points straight at the dialog and it opens and closes before any script runs.
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control.unlock: Modal dialogs always needed JS to open → plain HTML pages (docs, form confirmations, image lightboxes) get dialogs with native focus handling that still open if scripts break

mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control:2.title: Don't put both `popovertarget` and `commandfor` on one button
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control:2.action: Use either `popovertarget` or `commandfor` to control a given popover, not both
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control:2.blocker: Using both toggles the popover twice and breaks it (quote: "This will double-toggle it, breaking functionality.")
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control:2.outcome: With only one, the popover opens and closes normally (official claim)
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control:2.story: Both declarative toggles do the same job; stack them and it opens and immediately closes.

mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control:3.title: When closing a popover from inside it, return focus to the trigger
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control:3.action: When a `hide-popover` button inside the popover closes it, add script that moves focus back to the button that opened it
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control:3.blocker: The close button is hidden along with the popover and focus is lost (quote: "will result in a loss of focus as the button will be hidden and won't retain focus")
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control:3.outcome: People can continue from where they were (official claim)
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control:3.story: The moment you press "Close", that button disappears too, and keyboard users are dropped back at the top of the page.

mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control:4.title: With the popover polyfill, don't set the `popover` property and wrap `:popover-open` in `:is()`
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control:4.action: Before the polyfill loads, use `setAttribute()` / `removeAttribute()` for popover; write styles as `[popover]:is(:popover-open, .\:popover-open)`; load the polyfill only when `HTMLElement.prototype` lacks `popover`
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control:4.blocker: Setting the IDL property before the polyfill loads means the element is never picked up and the polyfill's accessor is shadowed forever; a bare `:popover-open` makes browsers that don't know it drop the whole rule (quote: "otherwise browsers that lack `:popover-open` discard the entire rule")
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control:4.outcome: Older browsers get working popovers and open-state styles through the polyfill (official claim)
mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control:4.story: The polyfill can't create a real pseudo-class or intercept a property set too early; write it the native way and in older browsers the popover won't open or won't be styled.

mwg:directional-navigation-transitions.title: Give SPA navigation forward/back direction with typed view transitions
mwg:directional-navigation-transitions.action: Pass `forward` / `backward` to `document.startViewTransition({ update, types: [direction] })`, and in CSS apply matching `transform` slides with `html:active-view-transition-type(forward)::view-transition-old(root)`, using non-linear easing on `::view-transition-group(root)`
mwg:directional-navigation-transitions.blocker: SPA view changes just replace the content with no transition (quote: "By default, the content is simply replaced, without any transitions.")
mwg:directional-navigation-transitions.outcome: New content slides in from the direction the user is moving, reinforcing the spatial relationship between views; view transitions and active view transition are both Newly (official claim)
mwg:directional-navigation-transitions.story: An SPA "next page" just swaps the content, and users can't feel where they're going. Passing direction as a transition type lets one set of CSS tell forward from back.
mwg:directional-navigation-transitions.unlock: Direction used to need an animation library plus state management → multi-step forms, slideshows (up/down), and product browsing (left/right) can pick the slide direction with one `types` argument
mwg:directional-navigation-transitions.support: View transitions: Newly (2025-10-14); Active view transition: Newly (2026-01-13)

mwg:directional-navigation-transitions:2.title: Still update the DOM when `startViewTransition` is missing
mwg:directional-navigation-transitions:2.action: Have the navigate function check `document.startViewTransition` and call `updateDOM()` directly when it doesn't exist
mwg:directional-navigation-transitions:2.blocker: In unsupported browsers `document.startViewTransition` is `undefined`; calling it without detection means the view never updates (quote: "In unsupported browsers, `document.startViewTransition` will be `undefined`.")
mwg:directional-navigation-transitions:2.outcome: Unsupported browsers still swap content immediately, just without animation (official claim)
mwg:directional-navigation-transitions:2.story: The transition is a bonus; the navigation isn't. Wrap the transition in detection so only the animation can fail.

mwg:drag.title: Remember the grab offset and clamp to the viewport so dragged elements don't jump or get lost
mwg:drag.action: Use `position: fixed` for the floating panel; start only on the primary button, record the pointer offset on `pointerdown`, use `setPointerCapture()` so the drag continues after the pointer leaves the handle; route pointer and arrow-key moves through one clamping helper and re-clamp when the viewport or element resizes
mwg:drag.blocker: Without the offset the element jumps when grabbed away from its corner; without clamping it can be dragged out of view and can't be retrieved (quote: "so the element does not jump when grabbed away from its corner", "so the element stays reachable")
mwg:drag.outcome: The element follows the pointer and always stays within the viewport, including keyboard moves (official claim)
mwg:drag.story: The first flaw in a drag is usually "it jumps when grabbed", the second "once it's off-screen you can't get it back". Offset and clamping live in one helper that the keyboard path shares.
mwg:drag.support: Pointer events / pointer capture: no support data in the guide, recorded as N/A

mwg:drag:2.title: Apply drag styles to the handle, not the whole element
mwg:drag:2.action: Put `cursor: grab`, `touch-action: none`, `-webkit-user-select: none`, and `user-select: none` only on a dedicated drag handle, a focusable `<button>` whose name mentions the arrow keys
mwg:drag:2.blocker: On the whole draggable element, text inside can't be selected and touch gestures lose their usual behavior; Safari doesn't support unprefixed `user-select` (quote: "so text outside it remains selectable and touch gestures retain their usual behavior")
mwg:drag:2.outcome: Panel content stays selectable and scrollable; `user-select` is Limited, and the `-webkit-` prefix keeps Safari from selecting text during drags (official claim)
mwg:drag:2.story: Make the whole panel unselectable and non-scrollable for the sake of dragging, and the notes and links inside stop working.
mwg:drag:2.support: user-select: Limited availability, Supported by: Chrome 54, Edge 79, Firefox 69; Unsupported in: Safari

mwg:dynamic-sibling-animations.title: Stagger list items into view with `sibling-index()`
mwg:dynamic-sibling-animations.action: `animation-delay: calc(sibling-index() * var(--stagger-time))` delays each item by its position; disable under reduced motion; for older browsers, first declare a version using a JS-set `--sibling-index`
mwg:dynamic-sibling-animations.blocker: The guide only describes the stagger effect, without saying when the old approaches (per-item `:nth-child` or JS delays) go wrong (quote: "multiple ordered elements animate sequentially with a slight delay between each, rather than all animating at once")
mwg:dynamic-sibling-animations.outcome: Delays are computed from position in pure CSS; `sibling-index()` is Newly, older browsers need a JS custom-property fallback (official claim)
mwg:dynamic-sibling-animations.story: Stagger delays used to come from JS or a long list of nth-child rules. Now CSS knows "which one am I", and adding or removing items needs no recalculation.
mwg:dynamic-sibling-animations.unlock: Staggered entrances needed JS to set each delay → search results, notification lists, and dashboard cards can appear one after another in pure CSS and stay in step when the count changes
mwg:dynamic-sibling-animations.support: sibling-count() and sibling-index(): Newly (2026-08-18), Supported by: Chrome 138, Edge 138, Firefox 154, Safari 26.2

mwg:group-element-transitions.title: Define a whole group's transition once with `view-transition-class`
mwg:group-element-transitions.action: Give each item a unique `view-transition-name` plus a shared `view-transition-class: list-item`; set duration and easing on `::view-transition-group(.list-item)`, and entry/exit on `::view-transition-new(.list-item):only-child` / `::view-transition-old(.list-item):only-child`; wrap DOM updates in `document.startViewTransition()`
mwg:group-element-transitions.blocker: The guide only says that without a class you repeat the transition logic for every name, without saying when the repetition causes an observable problem (quote: "define that logic once in CSS rather than repeating it for every unique `view-transition-name`")
mwg:group-element-transitions.outcome: A group shares one set of transition styles and adds, removes, and reorders all animate; both features are Newly, and without support the DOM updates without animation (official claim)
mwg:group-element-transitions.story: A list with dozens of items needs a name per item to be tracked, but the animation should be written once. The class separates "which is which" from "how it moves".
mwg:group-element-transitions.unlock: Animating list adds, removes, and reorders needed a FLIP library → to-do lists, shopping carts, and kanban columns can slide new items in, slide removed ones out, and close the gaps with one set of CSS

mwg:group-element-transitions:2.title: Keep non-transitioning elements interactive during a transition
mwg:group-element-transitions:2.action: Set `::view-transition { pointer-events: none; }` and, when only specific elements transition, `:root { view-transition-name: none; }` to disable the default root transition
mwg:group-element-transitions:2.blocker: During a transition the screen is an overlay of snapshots and elements can't be interacted with; the root transition animates between two identical full-page snapshots, so the whole page is unclickable (quote: "during the transition, elements are not interactive")
mwg:group-element-transitions:2.outcome: Controls not part of the transition stay clickable during the animation (official claim)
mwg:group-element-transitions:2.story: Only one list item is moving, yet every button on the page ignores clicks for that half second.

mwg:highlight-text-ranges.title: Highlight text with the CSS Custom Highlight API without touching the DOM
mwg:highlight-text-ranges.action: Collect text nodes with a `TreeWalker`, create `Range`s, wrap them in `new Highlight(...ranges)`, register with `CSS.highlights.set("search-results", h)`, and style with `::highlight(search-results)`; use `priority` for overlaps
mwg:highlight-text-ranges.blocker: The fallback of wrapping matches in `<mark>` modifies the DOM, so you must take care to keep event listeners and not break the document structure (quote: "This modifies the DOM, so take care to preserve event listeners and avoid breaking the document structure.")
mwg:highlight-text-ranges.outcome: Arbitrary text ranges can be styled with the DOM unchanged; custom highlights are Newly, with `<mark>` wrapping as the fallback (official claim)
mwg:highlight-text-ranges.story: In-page search, syntax coloring, and collaborative cursors used to split text into wrapper elements, and each split risked losing someone else's listeners and structure. Now ranges are just a registration and the browser paints the style.
mwg:highlight-text-ranges.unlock: Marking text used to mean splitting the DOM → a notes app's in-page search, live syntax coloring in code blocks, and other people's selections in collaborative editing can sit on top of framework-rendered content without conflict
mwg:highlight-text-ranges.support: Custom highlights: Newly (2026-03-24), Supported by: Chrome 105, Edge 105, Firefox 149, Safari 17.2

mwg:highlight-text-ranges:2.title: Use `<mark>` for meaningful highlights, not custom highlights
mwg:highlight-text-ranges:2.action: Reserve custom highlights for transient visuals like search results or syntax coloring; use `<mark>` when the highlight itself carries meaning; pair error highlights with a wavy underline, label, or icon
mwg:highlight-text-ranges:2.blocker: Custom highlights are purely presentational and not in the accessibility tree, so screen reader users miss whatever the highlight conveys (quote: "Custom highlights are purely presentational and are not exposed to the accessibility tree.")
mwg:highlight-text-ranges:2.outcome: Meaningful highlights reach assistive technology through `<mark>` (official claim)
mwg:highlight-text-ranges:2.story: The same yellow background is just a hint in search results but may be the key point in a tutorial; leave the latter to a highlight and screen reader users miss it.

mwg:highlight-text-ranges:3.title: Clear old highlights before registering new ones
mwg:highlight-text-ranges:3.action: Call `CSS.highlights.clear()` before each `set()`; cache the text-node list and rebuild it only when the DOM content changes
mwg:highlight-text-ranges:3.blocker: Without clearing, stale ranges stay on the page (quote: "to avoid stale ranges persisting on the page")
mwg:highlight-text-ranges:3.outcome: Only the current results are shown (official claim)
mwg:highlight-text-ranges:3.story: The search term changed but the previous term is still lit up; the registry doesn't expire on its own.

mwg:highlight-text-ranges:4.title: `::highlight()` only accepts a few properties
mwg:highlight-text-ranges:4.blocker: Properties such as `background-image`, `font-size`, or `padding` are ignored (quote: "Properties like `background-image`, `font-size`, or `padding` are ignored.")
mwg:highlight-text-ranges:4.outcome: Designing within the allowed properties makes the styles apply (official claim)
mwg:highlight-text-ranges:4.story: A highlight isn't an element and has no box; designs that bold, outline, or resize the text can't be done here.

mwg:interactive-content-reveal.title: Register gradient stops with `@property` so a pointer-following spotlight opens and closes smoothly
mwg:interactive-content-reveal.action: Register `--inner-size` and `--outer-size` as `<length-percentage>` with `@property`, reference them in `mask-image: radial-gradient(circle at var(--mouse-x) var(--mouse-y), …)`, transition only the sizes, and update only the position variables on `pointermove`
mwg:interactive-content-reveal.blocker: Browsers without `@property` can't interpolate values inside `radial-gradient`, so the spotlight snaps between on and off (quote: "the movement will jump between on and off states because they cannot interpolate values inside a `radial-gradient`")
mwg:interactive-content-reveal.outcome: The spotlight follows the pointer and grows and shrinks smoothly, with JS only updating coordinates; registered custom properties are Newly, and without them the spotlight still appears but jumps (official claim)
mwg:interactive-content-reveal.story: Numbers inside a gradient can't animate by default, so the spotlight could only pop in. Registering the stops as typed properties tells the browser how to transition between sizes.
mwg:interactive-content-reveal.unlock: Sizes inside gradients couldn't transition → a portfolio "flashlight over the sketch", a circular magnifier on before/after images, or an X-ray effect on product shots can open and close smoothly with just a little coordinate JS
mwg:interactive-content-reveal.support: Registered custom properties: Newly (2024-07-09); Masks: Widely

mwg:interactive-content-reveal:2.title: The spotlight is decoration only; it must not hide or gate content
mwg:interactive-content-reveal:2.action: Set `pointer-events: none` on the mask layer; keep the underlying content fully visible and keyboard-reachable by default, with the spotlight as an extra for pointer users
mwg:interactive-content-reveal:2.blocker: Using the effect to obscure or gate essential content leaves keyboard-only and assistive technology users without it, and the mask layer blocks clicks on controls beneath (quote: "Never use this effect to obscure or gate essential content from keyboard-only or assistive technology users.")
mwg:interactive-content-reveal:2.outcome: All content is visible and operable without a pointer, and clicks pass through to the layer below (official claim)
mwg:interactive-content-reveal:2.story: "Move over it to see" is fun, but only for mouse users; the content itself must be open to everyone first.
mwg:interactive-content-reveal:2.support: Accessibility requirement: no support data in the guide, recorded as N/A

mwg:interest-triggered-action-previews.title: Preview an action's effect before it's pressed with `interestfor`
mwg:interest-triggered-action-previews.action: Put `interestfor="target-id"` on a button or link, listen for `interest` / `loseinterest` on the target and apply or undo the preview based on `event.source`; style with `:interest-source` / `:interest-target`, tune delays with `interest-delay-start` / `-end`
mwg:interest-triggered-action-previews.blocker: The guide only says previewing actions before committing can help, without saying when older approaches go wrong (quote: "It can be beneficial to provide users a preview of their actions before they commit to them.")
mwg:interest-triggered-action-previews.outcome: One target can have several interest sources, and the preview appears on hover or focus and reverts on leave; interest invokers are Limited, other browsers need the conditionally loaded `interestfor` polyfill, with classes instead of pseudo-classes and CSS variables for delays (official claim)
mwg:interest-triggered-action-previews.story: Seeing the effect by hovering "Bold" or "Italic" used to mean wiring hover, focus, leave, and delays by hand. Now "interest" is a declared relationship, and the browser manages events and delays.
mwg:interest-triggered-action-previews.unlock: Previews needed hand-written hover/focus/delay handling → theme pickers, font menus, and filter buttons can "try it on while hovering, revert on leave", including on keyboard focus. Native in Chromium only, others via polyfill
mwg:interest-triggered-action-previews.support: Interest invokers: Limited availability, Supported by: Chrome 149, Edge 149; Unsupported in: Firefox, Safari

mwg:interest-triggered-action-previews:2.title: Don't announce interest-triggered previews in a live region
mwg:interest-triggered-action-previews:2.action: Let the preview be the affordance; don't announce apply/unapply through a live region
mwg:interest-triggered-action-previews:2.blocker: Interest fires just from moving the pointer or tabbing past nearby buttons, so apply/unapply announcements become noise that drowns out content users care about (quote: "apply/unapply announcements quickly become noise that can drown out content the user actually cares about")
mwg:interest-triggered-action-previews:2.outcome: Screen readers aren't flooded with preview noise (official claim)
mwg:interest-triggered-action-previews:2.story: Sweep the mouse across a row of buttons and the screen reader says "previewing" five times; people who can't see the preview gain nothing from hearing it.

mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips.title: Build tooltips that don't close menus with `popover="hint"` and `interestfor`
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips.action: Use `<div popover="hint" id>` for the tooltip and `interestfor` on the triggering `<button>` / `<a>`; the trigger becomes an implicit anchor, positioned with `position-area: block-start` and `position-try-fallbacks: flip-block`; toggletips also get `popovertarget` with `popovertargetaction="show"`
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips.blocker: With an `auto` popover as a tooltip, hovering across it closes an open menu (quote: "hovering across a toggletip must not close an open menu, which an `auto` popover would")
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips.outcome: Hints only close other hints and leave `auto`/`manual` popovers alone, with built-in light dismiss and Esc, and are wired to the accessible description or name based on their content; interest invokers and `popover="hint"` are both Limited, other browsers need polyfills (official claim; anchor positioning support adjusted per the verified deviation)
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips.story: Tooltips and menus are both popovers, so opening one used to close the other. `hint` is a third type for glance-and-go content, opened by hover, focus, or long-press without disturbing what's already open.
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips.unlock: Tooltips used to need hand-wired hover/focus/Esc and fought with menus → icon-button help, term definitions, and link preview cards can be almost fully declarative and readable while a menu is open. Native in Chromium only, others via polyfill
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips.support: Interest invokers: Limited (Chrome 149, Edge 149); popover="hint": Limited (Chrome 151, Edge 151, Firefox 153; Unsupported in: Safari); Anchor positioning core properties: Newly. The guide says "Supported by: Safari 27 (Sep 2026). Unsupported in: Chrome, Edge, and Firefox.", which is the misleading group status, see `lines/ui-components/app-menus.md`; this line doesn't use `position-visibility`

mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:2.title: Don't add `aria-expanded` to triggers that do something else
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:2.action: When the trigger navigates or performs an action (a link, a button with its own action), give the hint `role="tooltip"` and the trigger `aria-describedby`, not `aria-expanded`; only toggletips that open the hint on press use `aria-expanded`, synced from the popover's `toggle` event
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:2.blocker: A trigger announced as "collapsed" suggests Enter will expand it, but Enter navigates or acts (quote: "A trigger announced as "collapsed" suggests `Enter` would expand it, but `Enter` navigates or acts.")
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:2.outcome: What the screen reader announces matches what pressing does (official claim)
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:2.story: Browsers and screen readers don't yet expose `interestfor` semantics consistently, so you add ARIA yourself; add one wrong `aria-expanded` and a link is announced as something expandable.

mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:3.title: Add nothing when the hint matches the accessible name
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:3.action: Normalize whitespace and compare the hint text with the trigger's accessible name; if equal, add no description; only when the trigger has no name, point `aria-labelledby` at the hint
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:3.blocker: For example an icon button with `aria-label="Bold"` and a "Bold" tooltip: a description identical to the name is read twice (quote: "A description identical to the name would be read twice.")
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:3.outcome: Each name is read once (official claim)
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:3.story: The most common tooltip text is the button's own name; wire it up as a description too and the screen reader says "Bold, Bold".

mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:4.title: Hints exposed as descriptions may only hold content that's fine to miss
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:4.action: Put only skippable content such as link previews or action descriptions in description hints; information users need goes in a toggletip or inline
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:4.blocker: Not every screen reader reads descriptions while browsing; NVDA skips them in browse mode by design (quote: "Not every screen reader reads descriptions when moving through the page (NVDA skips them in browse mode by design)")
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:4.outcome: Essential information isn't lost when a screen reader skips descriptions (official claim)
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:4.story: Put "why this field is required" in a hover hint and sighted users occasionally see it, while NVDA users never hear it.

mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:5.title: `toggle` doesn't bubble: sync `aria-expanded` with a capturing listener
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:5.action: Handle popover `toggle` events with a single capturing listener on `document` and update every trigger pointing at that hint; treat the popover as the source of truth instead of syncing from `interest` / `loseinterest`
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:5.blocker: `toggle` doesn't bubble, so a normal listener on `document` never fires; the popover can also be closed by Esc, light dismiss, or another invoker (quote: "A bubbling listener on `document` never fires; use the capture phase (or a listener per popover).")
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:5.outcome: However the hint closes, `aria-expanded` follows the popover's real state (official claim)
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:5.story: Syncing from interest events seems enough, until Esc closes the hint and the trigger still announces "expanded".

mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:6.title: Without `hint` support, switch toggletips to `auto` in `beforetoggle`
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:6.action: Detect support by setting `popover = "hint"` on a probe element and reading it back; if unsupported, in a capturing `beforetoggle` listener switch the opening toggletip to `popover = "auto"`
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:6.blocker: Browsers without `hint` treat it as `manual`: a tooltip opened by keyboard focus can stay open when another is opened by hover, and a click-opened toggletip has no interest to lose and never closes (quote: "so a `manual` fallback would never close")
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:6.outcome: In Safari toggletips can still be closed by light dismiss or Esc (official claim)
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:6.story: An invalid attribute value silently becomes `manual`: it opens but won't close. The type has to change in `beforetoggle`; changing it while open closes it.

mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:7.title: Without the anchor positioning polyfill, gate `inset: auto` inside `@supports`
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:7.action: Without the polyfill, put `inset: auto`, `margin: 0`, and `position-area` inside `@supports (position-area: block-end)`, or give a `@supports not` fixed bottom bar; with the polyfill, set explicit `anchor-name` / `position-anchor` on each trigger and hint pair because the polyfill doesn't support implicit anchors
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:7.blocker: Setting `inset: auto` unconditionally overrides the popover's default centering while `position-area` is ignored, leaving the tooltip in the top-left corner or over its trigger (quote: "leaving the popover stranded at `(0, 0)` or overlapping its trigger")
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:7.outcome: Unsupported browsers at least keep the default centering or a bottom bar instead of a stuck corner (official claim; anchor positioning support adjusted per the verified deviation)
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:7.story: The inset reset meant to pin the tooltip to its button leaves only the "reset" half in browsers that don't understand anchors.
mwg:interest-triggered-tooltips:7.support: Anchor positioning core properties: Newly (misleading group status, see `lines/ui-components/app-menus.md`; this line doesn't use `position-visibility`)

mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog.title: Use closedby="any" to dismiss a modal dialog from its backdrop
mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog.action: Open <dialog closedby="any"> with showModal(). Where unsupported, fall back to a script that checks coordinates only when the event target is the dialog itself.
mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog.blocker: With hand-written light dismissal, clicking the dialog background or padding also targets the dialog, so a target-only check closes it by mistake. (quote: "This distinguishes between a click on the backdrop vs a click on the dialog's background/padding.")
mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog.outcome: One attribute provides backdrop, Escape, and programmatic dismissal; closedby is Limited, so Safari still needs the coordinate-checking fallback.
mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog.story: Backdrop and dialog padding look alike to a click handler. Native light dismissal removes that ambiguity.
mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog.unlock: Image lightboxes, quick previews, and settings panels can gain native-feeling dismissal with one attribute instead of coordinate calculations. Safari still needs the fallback.
mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog.support: <dialog closedby>: Limited; Chrome/Edge 134 and Firefox 141, unsupported in Safari.

mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog:2.title: Let nested components handle Escape before the dialog
mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog:2.action: Menus and comboboxes inside a modal dialog should handle Escape while focused.
mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog:2.blocker: A component tries to close its list with Escape but inadvertently closes the whole dialog. (quote: "this may lead to the dialog being inadvertently closed")
mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog:2.outcome: The focused component receives Escape first and the dialog stays open.
mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog:2.story: Pressing Escape to cancel a selection should not make a half-completed form disappear.
mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog:2.support: Modal dialog Escape behavior: no support data in the guide; N/A.

mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog:3.title: closedby only works for dialogs opened with showModal()
mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog:3.action: Use showModal() whenever backdrop dismissal is required; do not rely on closedby for non-modal dialogs opened with show().
mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog:3.blocker: A non-modal dialog has no backdrop and does not trigger light dismissal. (quote: "as they do not have a backdrop and won't trigger light-dismiss")
mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog:3.outcome: Modal opening supplies the backdrop, focus containment, and Escape behavior.
mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog:3.story: The attribute can be present but appear broken because the dialog has no outside backdrop layer.

mwg:motion.title: Draw focus on the parent when clipping or masking a focusable element
mwg:motion.action: When clip-path or mask-image reveals a focusable element, put its focus indicator on an unclipped parent.
mwg:motion.blocker: Clipping and masking also clip the element's own focus outline. (quote: "Both also clip the element's own focus outline")
mwg:motion.outcome: The effect no longer removes the focus indicator.
mwg:motion.story: A fade at the edges can otherwise fade away the keyboard user's only position cue.
mwg:motion.support: clip-path and mask-image: no support data in the guide; N/A.

mwg:motion:2.title: Use scroll-driven animations for non-essential scroll effects
mwg:motion:2.action: Implement decorative scroll-linked effects with animation-timeline: scroll().
mwg:motion:2.blocker: The guide recommends replacing JS listeners but does not identify an observable failure. (quote: "Use **Scroll-Driven Animations** (`animation-timeline: scroll()`) for non-essential scroll-bound effects instead of JS listeners.")
mwg:motion:2.outcome: The guide does not state what improves after switching.
mwg:motion:2.story: This overview points to the detailed scroll progress and parallax guides.
mwg:motion:2.unlock: Progress bars, parallax, and scroll reveals can be tied directly to scroll position in CSS.
mwg:motion:2.support: No support data in this guide; N/A.

mwg:motion:3.title: Use View Transitions between complex layout states
mwg:motion:3.action: Animate substantial layout-state changes with View Transitions.
mwg:motion:3.blocker: The guide only says transitions can be seamless, without an observable failure in the old approach. (quote: "Use **View Transitions** to animate between complex layout states seamlessly.")
mwg:motion:3.story: This overview points to the grouped-element and directional-navigation transition guides.
mwg:motion:3.unlock: List and grid reordering can move each item smoothly to its new position.
mwg:motion:3.support: No support data in this guide; N/A.

mwg:motion:4.title: Declare transition-behavior separately after transition
mwg:motion:4.action: List opacity, display, and overlay in transition, then declare transition-behavior: allow-discrete on a later line.
mwg:motion:4.blocker: Putting it in or before the shorthand resets it or breaks it in older browsers. (quote: "Separate after transition so the shorthand doesn't reset it or fail in older browsers")
mwg:motion:4.outcome: Discrete entry and exit properties can transition while older browsers retain the other transitions.
mwg:motion:4.story: The same shorthand-reset trap appears in the element entry and exit guide.
mwg:motion:4.support: No support data in this guide; N/A.

mwg:motion:5.title: Do not add aria-pressed when the pause button label already changes
mwg:motion:5.action: Provide a keyboard-operable pause button for motion lasting over five seconds; when its label switches between Pause and Play, omit aria-pressed.
mwg:motion:5.blocker: Combining a changing label with aria-pressed makes screen readers announce a pressed Play button. (quote: "or screen readers announce a pressed "Play" button")
mwg:motion:5.outcome: The button name describes the state without contradiction.
mwg:motion:5.story: A pressed Play button leaves listeners unable to tell whether playback is active.
mwg:motion:5.support: ARIA usage: no support data in the guide; N/A.

mwg:motion:6.title: Leave content in its final state when animation is disabled
mwg:motion:6.action: Default to static content and add animation only under no-preference, ensuring elements end in their final state.
mwg:motion:6.blocker: Disabled animation can leave content at its initial hidden state, such as opacity: 0, including focus and selection indicators. (quote: "so content isn't left hidden (for example, at `opacity: 0`)")
mwg:motion:6.outcome: Content and indicators remain visible regardless of motion preference.
mwg:motion:6.story: If a fade-in starts transparent, disabling the animation must not leave it transparent forever.
mwg:motion:6.support: prefers-reduced-motion: no support data in the guide; N/A.

mwg:motion:7.title: Get the Animation object from event.animation
mwg:motion:7.action: Use event.animation in animation and transition events; feature-detect with animation in AnimationEvent.prototype.
mwg:motion:7.blocker: Filtering event.target.getAnimations() by name misses unnamed WAAPI animations, conflates same-name animations, and cannot distinguish pseudo-elements. (quote: "`event.target` always points to the originating DOM element, so it does not distinguish between animations running on the element itself versus one of its pseudo-elements")
mwg:motion:7.outcome: The exact animation that emitted the event is available, with pseudo-element identity in effect.pseudoElement.
mwg:motion:7.story: Name lookup fails when an element and its ::before both run a fade-in.
mwg:motion:7.support: event.animation: feature detection is given but no support data; N/A.

mwg:motion:8.title: Do not wait only for animationend when reduced motion disables animation
mwg:motion:8.action: When cleanup depends on animation completion, continue immediately if getAnimations() returns an empty list or retain a short opacity transition.
mwg:motion:8.blocker: With animation disabled, none, or zero duration, animationend and transitionend never fire, so dependent removal or hiding never happens. (quote: "`animationend` and `transitionend` never fire")
mwg:motion:8.outcome: Removal and hiding work regardless of motion preference.
mwg:motion:8.story: A notification cannot close if its close logic waits for an event that reduced motion prevents.
mwg:motion:8.support: No support data in the guide; N/A.

mwg:move-dom-element-without-losing-stat.title: Move elements with moveBefore() without reloading iframes or losing focus
mwg:move-dom-element-without-losing-stat.action: Replace appendChild() or insertBefore() with newParent.moveBefore(element, null), feature-detect it, and fall back to insertBefore().
mwg:move-dom-element-without-losing-stat.blocker: Traditional moves remove and reinsert nodes, reloading iframes, restarting CSS animations, and blurring inputs. (quote: "causing `<iframe>` elements to reload, CSS animations to restart, and input fields to lose focus")
mwg:move-dom-element-without-losing-stat.outcome: Atomic movement preserves state; moveBefore() is Limited, so Safari still resets state with the fallback.
mwg:move-dom-element-without-losing-stat.story: Moving a playing video or partly completed form no longer needs to recreate it.
mwg:move-dom-element-without-losing-stat.unlock: A video can move into a corner player and back without interruption, and embedded maps or chats can switch containers. Safari still resets them.
mwg:move-dom-element-without-losing-stat.support: moveBefore(): Limited; Chrome/Edge 133 and Firefox 144, unsupported in Safari.

mwg:move-dom-element-without-losing-stat.title: Implement connectedMoveCallback() for moved custom elements
mwg:move-dom-element-without-losing-stat.action: Put location-dependent custom-element updates in connectedMoveCallback().
mwg:move-dom-element-without-losing-stat.blocker: moveBefore() fires neither connectedCallback nor disconnectedCallback, so logic in those callbacks does not run. (quote: "their `connectedCallback` and `disconnectedCallback` lifecycle methods will **not** be fired")
mwg:move-dom-element-without-losing-stat.outcome: A dedicated callback updates state associated with the new location.
mwg:move-dom-element-without-losing-stat.story: Atomic movement removes the DOM-connection signal that some components use to initialize against their parent.

mwg:parallax-scroll-effects.title: Build layered parallax with view-timeline and sibling-index()
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects.action: Give the wrapper a view-timeline, bind each layer to it, and use sibling-index() to offset translation or animation ranges.
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects.blocker: The guide says native CSS is more performant than scroll listeners or IntersectionObserver but gives no observable failure. (quote: "In browsers with built-in support for scroll-driven animations, ALWAYS use the native CSS implementation as those are more performant.")
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects.outcome: Layers move at different speeds without hand-written values for each layer; both features are Newly and old browsers omit the decorative effect.
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects.story: Each layer shares a view timeline while its sibling index determines its speed.
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects.unlock: Campaign pages, product stories, and interactive picture books can add parallax layers whose speeds redistribute automatically in pure CSS.
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects.support: Scroll-driven animations: Newly (2026-10-27); sibling-index(): Newly via the sibling animations guide.

mwg:parallax-scroll-effects:2.title: Include animation-range when detecting scroll-driven animations
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects:2.blocker: Checking animation-timeline alone admits browsers with only partial support. (quote: "The `(animation-range: entry)` check **MUST** be included here, to filter out browsers with only partial support.")
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects:2.outcome: Partially supporting browsers take the fallback instead of producing a broken effect.
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects:2.story: Timeline support without range support is not full support.

mwg:parallax-scroll-effects:3.title: Declare animation-timeline and animation-range after the animation shorthand
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects:3.action: Write the animation shorthand first, followed by animation-timeline and animation-range.
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects:3.blocker: A later shorthand resets the timeline. (quote: "declare `animation-timeline` and `animation-range` *after* it to prevent the shorthand from resetting the timeline")
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects:3.story: This is the same shorthand-reset trap as the scroll progress indicator guide.

mwg:parallax-scroll-effects:4.title: Check reduced-motion preference in the JavaScript parallax fallback
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects:4.action: Use matchMedia to skip the fallback when the user prefers reduced motion.
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects:4.blocker: The CSS media query cannot affect inline styles set by the script, so the fallback still moves layers. (quote: "The `prefers-reduced-motion` media query in the CSS doesn't affect the inline styles the script sets")
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects:4.outcome: People preferring reduced motion avoid parallax in old browsers too.
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects:4.story: The CSS version respects the preference while inline JS styles would otherwise bypass it.
mwg:parallax-scroll-effects:4.support: Scroll-driven animations: Newly; this fallback targets unsupported browsers.

mwg:persistent-top-layer-ui.title: Move open dialogs, popovers, and fullscreen elements with moveBefore()
mwg:persistent-top-layer-ui.action: Move open top-layer elements with moveBefore(); in the fallback, record their state and reopen dialogs or popovers after insertion.
mwg:persistent-top-layer-ui.blocker: Removal and reinsertion abruptly close open modals, popovers, and fullscreen elements. (quote: "This removal resets the state, causing open modals, popovers, and fullscreen elements to close abruptly.")
mwg:persistent-top-layer-ui.outcome: Atomic movement keeps top-layer UI open; Safari must reopen it and has no equivalent fullscreen reopening path.
mwg:persistent-top-layer-ui.story: Layout restructuring no longer has to make the visible dialog disappear.
mwg:persistent-top-layer-ui.unlock: Fullscreen video and open dialogs can survive layout regrouping such as collapsing sidebars or splitting panes. Safari still closes them.
mwg:persistent-top-layer-ui.support: moveBefore(): Limited; Chrome/Edge 133 and Firefox 144, unsupported in Safari.

mwg:physics-based-easing.title: Create spring and bounce easing with linear() stops
mwg:physics-based-easing.action: Convert a JS easing function or SVG path into linear() stops, store them in a custom property, and supply a duration.
mwg:physics-based-easing.blocker: Simple ease-in and cubic-bezier() curves cannot express bounces or springs. (quote: "making it impossible to create complex physics-based effects like bounces or springs")
mwg:physics-based-easing.outcome: Enough straight-line stops approximate smooth springs and bounces; linear() is Widely available.
mwg:physics-based-easing.story: Overshoot-and-return motion can now be described as CSS points instead of a JS animation library.

mwg:physics-based-easing:2.title: Do not apply overshooting bounce curves to opacity
mwg:physics-based-easing:2.action: Use curves that overshoot 0–1 on transform or scale, not opacity.
mwg:physics-based-easing:2.blocker: Opacity flickers jarringly when values overshoot below 0 or above 1. (quote: "can cause visually jarring flickering if the value overshoots below 0 or above 1")
mwg:physics-based-easing:2.story: The overshoot that makes a spring useful has no meaningful opacity equivalent.

mwg:platform-controls-dismiss-dialog.title: Let modal dialogs respond to back buttons and back gestures
mwg:platform-controls-dismiss-dialog.action: Open dialogs with showModal() or command="show-modal"; the default close-request behavior handles platform dismissal, with closedby="any" for backdrop dismissal.
mwg:platform-controls-dismiss-dialog.blocker: Early dialogs responded to Escape but not mobile back controls, and there was no good way to implement those close requests manually. (quote: "it could be dismissed with the <kbd>Esc</kbd> key, but not other platform controls such as a back button/gesture on mobile … There is no good way to implement close requests from mobile back button/gestures")
mwg:platform-controls-dismiss-dialog.outcome: Existing modal dialogs respond to back and assistive-technology dismissal gestures without code changes; Safari still only supports Escape.
mwg:platform-controls-dismiss-dialog.story: Mobile back now closes the dialog instead of navigating away from the whole page.
mwg:platform-controls-dismiss-dialog.unlock: Mobile filters, image viewers, and confirmations can close like native app surfaces without leaving the page. Safari is still unsupported.
mwg:platform-controls-dismiss-dialog.support: <dialog closedby>: Limited; Chrome/Edge 134 and Firefox 141, unsupported in Safari.

mwg:rich-media-picker.title: Use base-select for rich options instead of a custom menu
mwg:rich-media-picker.action: Set appearance: base-select on select and its picker; put SVG, images, titles, and descriptions in options, and mirror the selected content in the button.
mwg:rich-media-picker.blocker: Native option markup was stripped to plain text, forcing heavy custom components for rich options. (quote: "Prior to this API, the browser would strip tags from `<option>` tags and render only plain text.")
mwg:rich-media-picker.outcome: Supporting browsers retain native keyboard and form behavior; Firefox falls back to text-only system menus.
mwg:rich-media-picker.story: Rich options no longer require abandoning native select.
mwg:rich-media-picker.unlock: Assignee menus with avatars, color swatches, and plan descriptions can use native select and form submission. Firefox falls back to plain text.
mwg:rich-media-picker.support: Customizable select: Limited; Chrome/Edge 135 and Safari 27, unsupported in Firefox.

mwg:rich-media-picker:2.title: Make option text understandable without its visual layout
mwg:rich-media-picker:2.action: Add visually hidden punctuation and connecting phrases so option text reads coherently as plain text.
mwg:rich-media-picker:2.blocker: Unsupported browsers concatenate all option text into one line and lose the intended meaning. (quote: "would be rendered as "Frontend Developer React, Vue, CSS", in a browser that doesn't support customizable selects.")
mwg:rich-media-picker:2.outcome: Hidden punctuation restores understandable fallback text and screen-reader pauses, but not the rich layout.
mwg:rich-media-picker:2.story: The same option remains meaningful with or without customizable select support.

mwg:rich-media-picker:3.title: Do not override option text with aria-label
mwg:rich-media-picker:3.action: Let the complete option text provide its own accessible name instead of replacing it with aria-label.
mwg:rich-media-picker:3.blocker: aria-label overrides option text, so visible text omitted from the label is not announced and the two can drift. (quote: "This will result in people missing visible text that hasn't been included in the `aria-label`.")
mwg:rich-media-picker:3.outcome: Screen readers hear the complete visible text, within customizable-select support limits.
mwg:rich-media-picker:3.story: A separate label creates a second source of truth and loses information.

mwg:rich-media-picker:4.title: Do not put interactive elements inside option
mwg:rich-media-picker:4.action: Keep links, buttons, and other interactive semantics out of options; use static text and images only.
mwg:rich-media-picker:4.blocker: Screen-reader users do not hear interactive elements inside options and cannot tell that more information is present. (quote: "People using screen readers will not hear the announcements, and as a result, won't be able to determine that further information is present.")
mwg:rich-media-picker:4.outcome: Static content keeps the announced and visible information aligned.
mwg:rich-media-picker:4.story: Put additional interactive information outside the select.

mwg:rich-media-picker:5.title: Give base-select an explicit width
mwg:rich-media-picker:5.action: Set a fixed width or flex/grid constraints after enabling appearance: base-select.
mwg:rich-media-picker:5.blocker: base-select removes longest-option sizing, so the select changes width with the selected content and shifts layout. (quote: "Setting `appearance: base-select` removes the default browser behavior of sizing the select based on its longest option width.")
mwg:rich-media-picker:5.outcome: An explicit width stabilizes the layout.
mwg:rich-media-picker:5.story: Native select reserves width for its longest option; customizable select does not.

mwg:select-menu-interaction.title: Use select:user-invalid to delay required-select errors
mwg:select-menu-interaction.action: Give the first option an empty disabled value and trigger errors with :user-invalid and success with :user-valid.
mwg:select-menu-interaction.blocker: Standard validation marks an empty default option invalid on page load, creating visual noise. (quote: "standard validation flags the field as invalid immediately if the default option has an empty value. This can create visual noise.")
mwg:select-menu-interaction.outcome: The field stays neutral until the user changes it and leaves, or attempts submission.
mwg:select-menu-interaction.story: Errors appear only after meaningful interaction; browser differences still require device testing.

mwg:slider.title: Calculate slider fill in CSS with progress() and attr()
mwg:slider.action: Read min and max with typed attr(), calculate the percentage with progress(), and feed it to the track gradient; use ::-moz-range-progress in Firefox.
mwg:slider.blocker: WebKit/Blink has no filled-track pseudo-element, so scripts must synchronize values to style filled and unfilled portions. (quote: "WebKit/Blink do not provide an equivalent pseudo-element, so sync the live input value to `--control-value` on `input` events")
mwg:slider.outcome: CSS reads bounds and computes the ratio; Safari still needs JS for bounds and older browsers need calc().
mwg:slider.story: Only the current value still needs JavaScript synchronization.
mwg:slider.unlock: Volume, rating thresholds, and budget sliders can keep ratio calculations in CSS and change bounds through HTML attributes. Safari needs a JS fallback.
mwg:slider.support: progress(): Newly; typed attr(): Limited, unsupported in Safari.

mwg:slider:2.title: Write WebKit and Firefox slider pseudo-elements in separate rules
mwg:slider:2.action: Use separate rule blocks for ::-webkit-slider-thumb and ::-moz-range-thumb, and likewise for tracks.
mwg:slider:2.blocker: A selector list containing an unrecognized vendor pseudo-element is dropped in full. (quote: "browsers drop the entire rule if an unrecognized vendor pseudo-element is encountered.")
mwg:slider:2.outcome: Each engine ignores only its own unsupported block and applies the other.
mwg:slider:2.story: Combining prefixed pseudo-elements makes the styling fail in both engines.
mwg:slider:2.support: No support data for prefixed pseudo-elements; N/A.

mwg:sms-otp-form.title: Use WebOTP and domain-bound SMS to autofill verification codes
mwg:sms-otp-form.action: Use one one-time-code input, put @domain #code in the SMS, retrieve it with navigator.credentials.get(), submit with requestSubmit(), and abort on exit paths.
mwg:sms-otp-form.blocker: Switching apps to memorize or copy a code adds friction and drop-off and enables phishing on spoofed domains. (quote: "Switching between a browser and an SMS messaging app to memorize or copy-paste a multi-digit code introduces user friction, increases drop-off rates, and leaves users vulnerable to phishing on spoofed domains.")
mwg:sms-otp-form.outcome: Supporting browsers verify the domain and fill the code in one click; others use keyboard suggestions or manual numeric input.
mwg:sms-otp-form.story: Domain binding prevents autofill on a spoofed page and WebOTP removes app switching.
mwg:sms-otp-form.unlock: Phone verification and payment confirmation can autofill and submit when SMS arrives, without exposing automatic fill to phishing pages. Cross-origin iframes remain Chromium-only for delegation.
mwg:sms-otp-form.support: WebOTP: Limited; Chrome/Edge 93 and Safari 27, unsupported in Firefox.

mwg:sms-otp-form:2.title: Use text plus inputmode="numeric" for OTP, not type="number"
mwg:sms-otp-form:2.action: Use type="text" with inputmode="numeric" and a digit pattern for verification codes.
mwg:sms-otp-form:2.blocker: Number inputs add spinners, can strip leading zeros, and allow scroll-wheel changes. (quote: "Using `type="number"` adds increment/decrement spinner buttons, can strip leading zeros, and allows accidental scroll-wheel value changes.")
mwg:sms-otp-form:2.outcome: Mobile still shows a numeric keyboard while the value remains an exact string.
mwg:sms-otp-form:2.story: A code is an identifier, not a quantity.

mwg:sms-otp-form:3.title: Use one OTP field instead of six boxes
mwg:sms-otp-form:3.action: Use one input and create a segmented appearance with monospace type and letter-spacing.
mwg:sms-otp-form:3.blocker: Six separate inputs break native one-time-code autofill, hinder pasting, and complicate screen-reader navigation. (quote: "Multi-box OTP patterns (six separate `maxlength="1"` inputs) break native `autocomplete="one-time-code"` autofill in many browsers, hinder copy-pasting, and complicate screen reader navigation.")
mwg:sms-otp-form:3.outcome: One field supports system suggestions and whole-code pasting while retaining the segmented appearance.
mwg:sms-otp-form:3.story: The visual design no longer determines the input architecture.
mwg:sms-otp-form:3.support: inputmode: Widely; no support data for one-time-code autocomplete.

mwg:sms-otp-form:4.title: Use requestSubmit() after automatic OTP retrieval
mwg:sms-otp-form:4.action: Fill the code and call form.requestSubmit(), or call the validation routine directly.
mwg:sms-otp-form:4.blocker: form.submit() bypasses submit listeners and native constraint validation. (quote: "`form.submit()` bypasses `submit` event listeners (`event.preventDefault()` / `fetch()` handlers) and skips native constraint validation.")
mwg:sms-otp-form:4.outcome: requestSubmit() follows the same listener and validation path as a user-initiated submission.
mwg:sms-otp-form:4.story: Automatic retrieval no longer skips the application's normal submission logic.
mwg:sms-otp-form:4.support: No support data for requestSubmit(); N/A.

mwg:sms-otp-form:5.title: Place OTP format hints above the input
mwg:sms-otp-form:5.action: Link persistent format instructions with aria-describedby and place them visually above the input.
mwg:sms-otp-form:5.blocker: Autofill popovers and mobile keyboards cover hints placed below the input. (quote: "place any format instructions (linked via `aria-describedby`) visually **above** the `<input>` so autofill popovers and mobile virtual keyboards never cover the instructions.")
mwg:sms-otp-form:5.outcome: The instructions remain visible while the field is focused.
mwg:sms-otp-form:5.story: Moving the hint avoids both overlays at the moment the user needs it.
mwg:sms-otp-form:5.support: Layout placement; no support data, N/A.

mwg:switch.title: Build a native switch with <input type="checkbox" switch>
mwg:switch.action: Add the switch attribute to a labeled checkbox and conditionally load a polyfill where unsupported.
mwg:switch.blocker: The guide states native form, keyboard, and semantics benefits but gives no concrete custom-switch failure.
mwg:switch.outcome: Only Safari 17.4 supports it natively; Chrome, Edge, and Firefox need a polyfill for role, appearance, and dragging.
mwg:switch.story: A checkbox can expose native switch appearance and semantics, but support remains limited.
mwg:switch.unlock: Settings switches can be one HTML element with native submission, keyboard behavior, and semantics. Only Safari is native; other browsers need a polyfill.

mwg:validate-input-after-interaction.title: Use :user-invalid to report errors after editing
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction.action: Declare constraints with email type, pattern, and required; trigger error and success styles with :user-invalid and :user-valid.
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction.blocker: Standard :invalid styling reports errors while the user is still typing. (quote: "Standard `:invalid` styling results in an error state appearing immediately, frustrating the user.")
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction.outcome: Errors wait until edited blur or submission and clear as soon as the value is fixed.
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction.story: Typing stays neutral instead of turning red on every incomplete intermediate value.

mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:2.title: Hide satisfied rule lists with visibility, not collapsing layout
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:2.action: Use visibility: hidden on the valid field's rules list so its space remains reserved.
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:2.blocker: Collapsing on blur moves the submit button between mousedown and mouseup, losing the click. (quote: "collapsing the list on blur would move the submit button between mousedown and mouseup, and the click would be lost.")
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:2.outcome: The button remains stationary and the click submits normally.
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:2.story: Hiding without layout collapse prevents the pointer target from jumping.

mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:3.title: Give passwords an explicit error message, not just red rules
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:3.action: Provide a textual password error with an Error-labelled icon; use rule-list color only as reinforcement.
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:3.blocker: Turning rules red neither explains the problem nor conveys the change to screen readers. (quote: "Turning the rules list red doesn't say what is wrong, and screen readers don't convey the color change.")
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:3.outcome: Visual and screen-reader users both receive the failure in text.
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:3.story: Color alone leaves users to infer which requirement failed.

mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:4.title: Place format hints and password rules above the input
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:4.action: Put persistent hints and rule lists above their inputs and connect them with aria-describedby.
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:4.blocker: Autocomplete popovers and mobile keyboards cover hints below the input during editing. (quote: "Place format hints above the input so autocomplete popovers don't cover them during editing")
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:4.story: The instructions stay above both overlays.
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:4.support: Layout placement; no support data, N/A.

mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:5.title: Wrap fallback selectors in :is()
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:5.action: Use :is(:user-invalid, .user-invalid-fallback) instead of a plain comma-separated selector list.
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:5.blocker: One unsupported selector in a plain list drops the entire rule. (quote: "in a plain selector list, one unsupported selector drops the whole rule.")
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:5.outcome: The forgiving :is() list preserves fallback-class styling in browsers without :user-invalid.
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:5.story: The fallback no longer disappears alongside the unsupported new selector.
mwg:validate-input-after-interaction:5.support: :user-valid and :user-invalid: Widely; no support data for :is().

mwg:accessible-web-components.title: Use ARIA element references across shadow boundaries
mwg:accessible-web-components.action: Use ariaLabelledByElements and ariaDescribedByElements inside shadow trees to reference labels and descriptions in light DOM.
mwg:accessible-web-components.blocker: ID references resolve only within their own tree, so cross-boundary references are silently ignored. (quote: "An `id`-based attribute in the Light DOM cannot point at an `id` inside a shadow tree, and vice versa; the reference is silently ignored.")
mwg:accessible-web-components.outcome: Outward element references now work; inward references still need Reference Target, and unsupported browsers need aria-label text.
mwg:accessible-web-components.story: Controls inside components can use page-owned help and error text without moving it into shadow DOM.
mwg:accessible-web-components.unlock: Design-system inputs can accept consumer-owned labels, descriptions, and errors while keeping native controls encapsulated.

mwg:accessible-web-components:2.title: Do not use delegatesFocus when the host owns the role
mwg:accessible-web-components:2.action: Put host controls in the tab order in connectedCallback; use delegatesFocus only when wrapping an internal native control.
mwg:accessible-web-components:2.blocker: Combining delegatesFocus with host role and state moves focus inside and skips the host state. (quote: "Do not combine `delegatesFocus: true` with a role/state on the host, or focus will land on the inner element and skip the host's state.")
mwg:accessible-web-components:2.outcome: Focus lands on the semantic host so assistive technology announces its role and state.
mwg:accessible-web-components:2.story: Choose either host semantics or delegated focus, not both.

mwg:accessible-web-components:3.title: Set tabIndex in connectedCallback, not the constructor
mwg:accessible-web-components:3.action: Set a default tabIndex in connectedCallback only when the consumer has not supplied tabindex.
mwg:accessible-web-components:3.blocker: Setting tabIndex in the constructor throws when createElement creates the element. (quote: "setting tabIndex in the constructor throws on createElement")
mwg:accessible-web-components:3.outcome: Both markup and createElement construction work, and consumer values remain respected.
mwg:accessible-web-components:3.story: Constructor-time attributes are invalid; defer them until connection.

mwg:custom-elements.title: Handle moveBefore() with connectedMoveCallback
mwg:custom-elements.action: Define connectedMoveCallback so atomic moves run it instead of disconnect and connect callbacks.
mwg:custom-elements.blocker: Ordinary moves rerun expensive setup and teardown, resetting state, focus, and iframe or media playback. (quote: "this callback fires *instead of* `disconnectedCallback` → `connectedCallback`, so state, focus, and iframe/media playback survive the move.")
mwg:custom-elements.outcome: Atomic movement preserves state, focus, and playback.
mwg:custom-elements.story: Components can update only location-dependent state instead of rebuilding.
mwg:custom-elements.unlock: Player, map, and editor components can move between workspaces or pop out and return without reloading; support follows moveBefore().
mwg:custom-elements.support: No data in this guide; moveBefore() is Limited.

mwg:custom-elements:2.title: Make connectedCallback repeatable and clean up in disconnectedCallback
mwg:custom-elements:2.action: Make setup idempotent and remove global listeners, timers, and observers on disconnection.
mwg:custom-elements:2.blocker: connectedCallback runs on every insertion, so moves rerun setup and missing teardown leaks resources. (quote: "It fires on every insertion, so moving the element re-runs it.")
mwg:custom-elements:2.outcome: Moves and reinsertion neither duplicate listeners nor leak timers.
mwg:custom-elements:2.story: Design for repeated connection rather than one-time initialization.

mwg:custom-elements:3.title: Define lifecycle callbacks and observedAttributes before define()
mwg:custom-elements:3.action: Place all lifecycle methods and static observedAttributes on the class before customElements.define().
mwg:custom-elements:3.blocker: Registration reads these settings once; later additions are ignored and attributeChangedCallback never fires. (quote: "`attributeChangedCallback` never fires unless `observedAttributes` was already present at `define()` time.")
mwg:custom-elements:3.outcome: Attribute and lifecycle callbacks fire as expected.
mwg:custom-elements:3.story: Registration is a snapshot, not a live lookup.

mwg:custom-elements:4.title: Handle existing attributes and late children during upgrades
mwg:custom-elements:4.action: Call super() first, synchronize existing attributes on connection, and track later attributes and children with callbacks and slotchange.
mwg:custom-elements:4.blocker: Upgraded elements may already have attributes and children, while long child lists may still be parsing during connectedCallback. (quote: "the HTML parser can yield mid-parse of long child lists, so the callback sometimes runs before every child is attached.")
mwg:custom-elements:4.outcome: Event-driven synchronization initializes correctly regardless of upgrade timing.
mwg:custom-elements:4.story: Read current state and observe later arrivals instead of assuming one fixed timing.

mwg:custom-elements:5.title: Use delayed opacity for undefined elements instead of permanent hiding
mwg:custom-elements:5.action: Give :not(:defined) opacity zero with a delayed fade-in, scoped only to the affected elements.
mwg:custom-elements:5.blocker: Hard hiding leaves content invisible after failed or slow scripts; a body-wide guard lets one widget block the whole page. (quote: "so a failed or slow script never hides content for good.")
mwg:custom-elements:5.outcome: Content appears after the timeout even when scripts fail.
mwg:custom-elements:5.story: Fail open rather than allowing a styling guard to hide content forever.

mwg:form-associated-custom-elements.title: Use FACE and ElementInternals instead of hidden inputs
mwg:form-associated-custom-elements.action: Set formAssociated, use setFormValue() and setValidity(), and implement reset, disabled, and restore callbacks.
mwg:form-associated-custom-elements.blocker: The guide lists FACE benefits but gives no concrete hidden-input failure.
mwg:form-associated-custom-elements.outcome: The element submits and validates like a native control, including reset, disabled fieldsets, and restoration.
mwg:form-associated-custom-elements.story: The custom element itself participates in forms rather than synchronizing a hidden proxy.

mwg:form-associated-custom-elements:2.title: Disable internal controls only in formDisabledCallback
mwg:form-associated-custom-elements:2.action: Disable controls inside shadow DOM without setting disabled on the host.
mwg:form-associated-custom-elements:2.blocker: Setting host disabled leaves it permanently disabled after an ancestor fieldset is re-enabled. (quote: "Do NOT toggle `disabled` on `this`, or a `<fieldset disabled>` toggle will leave the host permanently stuck with its own `disabled` attribute.")
mwg:form-associated-custom-elements:2.outcome: The component restores normally with its fieldset and matches :disabled automatically.
mwg:form-associated-custom-elements:2.story: The fieldset cannot remove a host attribute added by the callback.

mwg:form-associated-custom-elements:3.title: Do not set accessible names directly through ElementInternals
mwg:form-associated-custom-elements:3.action: Use ElementInternals for roles and states but leave naming to the consumer unless the element has its own visible label.
mwg:form-associated-custom-elements:3.blocker: An internals-provided name can override consumer naming such as a label element. (quote: "this would likely override any accessible name set when using the custom element, such as by labelling the element using a HTML label's `for` attribute.")
mwg:form-associated-custom-elements:3.outcome: The consumer label remains the announced accessible name.
mwg:form-associated-custom-elements:3.story: Component defaults must not replace page-specific names.

mwg:html.title: Use dialog showModal() and closedby instead of hand-written modal behavior
mwg:html.action: Use dialog with showModal(), closedby="any", form method="dialog", and ::backdrop; use popover for non-modal UI.
mwg:html.blocker: The guide lists automatic focus containment, Escape, and dismissal benefits but gives no concrete hand-written failure.
mwg:html.outcome: The browser handles focus containment, Escape, backdrop dismissal, and return values.
mwg:html.story: Modal behavior moves into platform primitives while a visible close button remains necessary.

mwg:html:2.title: Use inert to remove hidden regions from tab order and the accessibility tree
mwg:html:2.action: Apply inert to off-canvas menus or background pages behind drawers and indicate the state visually.
mwg:html:2.blocker: The guide states inert behavior but no concrete failure when it is omitted.
mwg:html:2.outcome: Inert regions cannot be focused or announced.
mwg:html:2.story: One attribute disables an entire region without changing every tabindex.

mwg:html:3.title: Do not hide focusable elements with aria-hidden or presentation roles
mwg:html:3.action: Use aria-hidden and role none only on non-focusable content, never on interactive iframes or their ancestors.
mwg:html:3.blocker: Content can be hidden from assistive technology while remaining reachable by sequential keyboard navigation. (quote: "Hiding elements from the assistive technology tree while leaving them accessible to sequential keyboard navigation violates core accessibility heuristics.")
mwg:html:3.outcome: Keyboard-reachable content remains perceivable to screen readers.
mwg:html:3.story: A decorative wrapper must not silence an interactive descendant.

mwg:html:4.title: Avoid focus({preventScroll:true}) without validation
mwg:html:4.action: Allow focus to scroll by default and ensure the focused element is not obscured.
mwg:html:4.blocker: preventScroll can leave the focused element off-screen. (quote: "it can hide the focused element off-screen.")
mwg:html:4.outcome: The browser brings the focused element into view.
mwg:html:4.story: Users can otherwise type into an invisible field.

mwg:html:5.title: Make scrollable code blocks keyboard-focusable regions
mwg:html:5.action: Give scrollable pre elements tabindex="0", role="region", and an accessible name.
mwg:html:5.blocker: Without tab access, keyboard users cannot scroll to clipped code content. (quote: "adding `tabindex="0"` to the `<pre>` element if it becomes scrollable, allowing keyboard users to reach the content.")
mwg:html:5.outcome: Keyboard users can scroll with arrow keys and screen readers announce the region name.
mwg:html:5.story: Horizontal overflow no longer makes part of the example unreachable.

mwg:html:6.title: Do not use the title attribute for tooltips
mwg:html:6.action: Use a tooltip pattern that supports keyboard triggering and consistent screen-reader announcements.
mwg:html:6.blocker: title-based tooltips cannot be accessed with a keyboard. (quote: "DON'T use the `title` attribute to create tooltip effects, as these cannot be accessed using a keyboard.")
mwg:html:6.outcome: Keyboard and screen-reader users can access the tooltip content.
mwg:html:6.story: Hover-only explanations disappear for non-mouse users.

mwg:html:7.title: Do not lazy-load the hero image; prioritize it
mwg:html:7.action: Give the LCP image fetchpriority="high", preload CSS hero backgrounds, and reserve lazy loading for off-screen media.
mwg:html:7.blocker: Lazy-loading above-the-fold or hero images delays LCP. (quote: "DON'T apply `loading="lazy"` to above-the-fold or hero images. This delays LCP.")
mwg:html:7.outcome: The hero downloads early while only off-screen resources are delayed.
mwg:html:7.story: Blanket lazy loading also delays the most important image.

mwg:html:8.title: Set width and height on images and video
mwg:html:8.action: Declare dimensions on every img and video, and optionally on picture sources.
mwg:html:8.blocker: Media without dimensions expands only after loading and shifts layout. (quote: "DO specify `width` and `height` on all `` tags to preserve aspect ratio and prevent Layout Shifts (CLS).")
mwg:html:8.outcome: The browser reserves aspect-ratio space before media arrives.
mwg:html:8.story: Reserved space keeps the reading position stable.

mwg:html:9.title: Use specific autocomplete tokens instead of off
mwg:html:9.action: Use tokens such as email, street-address, and cc-number aligned with type and inputmode.
mwg:html:9.blocker: Browsers and password managers intentionally ignore autocomplete="off" on credential, address, and payment fields. (quote: "Browsers and password managers ignore it there by design.")
mwg:html:9.outcome: Specific tokens let autofill and password managers provide the correct values and actions.
mwg:html:9.story: off neither disables suggestions nor identifies the field correctly.

mwg:prerendering-custom-elements.title: Server-render shadow trees with Declarative Shadow DOM
mwg:prerendering-custom-elements.action: Place template shadowrootmode="open" as the host's first child and include component styles in the template.
mwg:prerendering-custom-elements.blocker: Script-created shadow trees lack structure and style before JS runs, causing FOUC. (quote: "DSD renders correctly on first paint only if styles ship inside the declarative template.")
mwg:prerendering-custom-elements.outcome: The parser supplies structure and styles before any JavaScript, including streamed rendering.
mwg:prerendering-custom-elements.story: First paint contains the finished component rather than unstyled text.

mwg:prerendering-custom-elements:2.title: Reuse the server shadow root during hydration
mwg:prerendering-custom-elements:2.action: Check this.shadowRoot before attachShadow() and attach behavior to existing server markup.
mwg:prerendering-custom-elements:2.blocker: Re-rendering discards server DOM and flashes. (quote: "do NOT re-render; that would discard the server's DOM and flash.")
mwg:prerendering-custom-elements:2.outcome: Server markup remains authoritative and the page does not repaint.
mwg:prerendering-custom-elements:2.story: Hydrate existing DOM instead of replacing it.

mwg:shadow-dom.title: Share adoptedStyleSheets across component instances
