mwg:shadow-dom.action: Create one CSSStyleSheet at module scope and adopt the same object in every shadow root.
mwg:shadow-dom.blocker: A style element is duplicated per instance and bloats the DOM at scale; links add requests and FOUC risk. (quote: "Duplicated per instance; bloats the DOM at scale.")
mwg:shadow-dom.outcome: All instances share one parsed sheet, at the cost of requiring JS and losing @import.
mwg:shadow-dom.story: Hundreds of instances no longer contain hundreds of identical style copies.

mwg:shadow-dom:2.title: Use slotchange and assignedElements() to detect slot content
mwg:shadow-dom:2.action: Listen for slotchange and inspect assignedElements() before toggling slot-dependent state.
mwg:shadow-dom:2.blocker: Whitespace text nodes fill the default slot, and children may not exist yet during connectedCallback. (quote: "Text nodes between elements (including pure whitespace) are assigned to the default slot, so a default slot is rarely truly "empty."")
mwg:shadow-dom:2.outcome: slotchange reliably signals initial and later assignments.
mwg:shadow-dom:2.story: Check assigned elements rather than assuming whitespace means real content.

mwg:styling-web-components.title: Theme components with inherited custom properties, not :host-context()
mwg:styling-web-components.action: Set public custom properties on ancestors and consume them with var() inside the component.
mwg:styling-web-components.blocker: Firefox and Safari refuse :host-context(), leaving it a Chromium-only dead end. (quote: "Firefox and Safari have declined to ship it and the CSSWG is leaning toward not developing it further — treat it as a Chromium-only dead end")
mwg:styling-web-components.outcome: Inherited custom properties cross shadow boundaries in every browser.
mwg:styling-web-components.story: The page and component exchange theme values without relying on a non-portable selector.

mwg:styling-web-components:2.title: Keep public custom properties unset on :host
mwg:styling-web-components:2.action: Define a private alias on :host that reads the public property with a fallback, and use the alias internally.
mwg:styling-web-components:2.blocker: A public property defined on :host can only be overridden by rules targeting the host, blocking ancestor inheritance. (quote: "A custom property *defined* on `:host` can only be overridden by rules targeting the host element specifically.")
mwg:styling-web-components:2.outcome: The public property can inherit from any ancestor and the default appears once.
mwg:styling-web-components:2.story: A private alias preserves the external override path.

mwg:styling-web-components:3.title: Set font: inherit on wrapped native controls
mwg:styling-web-components:3.action: Apply font: inherit and usually color: inherit to buttons, inputs, and selects inside shadow trees.
mwg:styling-web-components:3.blocker: Form controls use UA fonts rather than inheriting, so wrapped controls render in the platform font. (quote: "The wrapped control therefore renders in the platform font, not the page font, until you set `font: inherit`")
mwg:styling-web-components:3.story: The shadow boundary is not the cause; form controls simply do not inherit fonts by default.

mwg:styling-web-components:4.title: Expose internal control styling with ::part or custom properties
mwg:styling-web-components:4.action: Mark internal controls with part attributes, export nested parts, or pass values through custom properties.
mwg:styling-web-components:4.blocker: Host background, border, and padding style only the host box, not the control inside. (quote: "Setting `background`/`border`/`padding` on `:host` styles the host box, not the control inside it.")
mwg:styling-web-components:4.outcome: Consumers can style selected internal elements without knowing the full structure.
mwg:styling-web-components:4.story: Use an intentional styling channel instead of assuming host declarations cascade inside.

mwg:styling-web-components:5.title: Avoid display: contents when the host must be measurable
mwg:styling-web-components:5.action: Treat display: contents plus all: inherit as a tradeoff; use parts or custom properties when measurement and anchoring matter.
mwg:styling-web-components:5.blocker: A display: contents host has zero client rects, breaking anchor positioning, and all: inherit erases UA defaults. (quote: "`getBoundingClientRect()` and `getClientRects()` return zero for `display: contents` elements, so anchor positioning against the host is broken.")
mwg:styling-web-components:5.outcome: Arbitrary style forwarding remains possible but measurement and anchoring costs remain.
mwg:styling-web-components:5.story: Transparent wrappers without boxes cannot position attached UI.

mwg:styling-web-components:6.title: Give custom-element hosts a block box for container queries
mwg:styling-web-components:6.action: Set :host to display: block and container-type: inline-size before using @container.
mwg:styling-web-components:6.blocker: Custom elements default to inline, and size containment does not apply to inline or contents elements. (quote: "custom elements default to `display: inline` and size containment does not apply to `inline` or `contents` elements")
mwg:styling-web-components:6.outcome: The component responds to its own width in sidebars and full-width layouts.
mwg:styling-web-components:6.story: A single display declaration activates the containment context.

mwg:web-components.title: Wrap real native buttons instead of recreating semantics
mwg:web-components.action: Use custom elements only for encapsulated state or scripting needs, and wrap actual native controls when needed.
mwg:web-components.blocker: The guide calls semantic recreation a common misuse but gives no concrete failure.
mwg:web-components.outcome: Native focus, activation, and accessibility remain platform-provided.
mwg:web-components.story: CSS alone is enough when only appearance changes.

mwg:web-components:2.title: Use open shadow roots
mwg:web-components:2.blocker: Closed roots hide shadowRoot from page scripts, tests, and automated accessibility checkers. (quote: "`mode: 'closed'` hides `element.shadowRoot` from page scripts, test harnesses, and automated accessibility checkers that walk shadow trees.")
mwg:web-components:2.outcome: Tools and hydration scripts can traverse the shadow tree.
mwg:web-components:2.story: Encapsulation does not require hiding the root from tooling.

mwg:web-components:3.title: Avoid customized built-in elements using is="…"
mwg:web-components:3.action: Wrap native elements in autonomous custom elements instead of extending built-ins with is.
mwg:web-components:3.blocker: Safari has permanently declined customized built-in elements. (quote: "Avoid *customized built-in elements* (`extends HTMLButtonElement` with `is="…"`); Safari has permanently declined to ship them.")
mwg:web-components:3.outcome: Autonomous wrappers behave consistently across browsers.
mwg:web-components:3.story: The elegant is syntax never gains the extended behavior in Safari.

mwg:calculate-event-differentials.title: Calculate calendar-aware differences with ZonedDateTime since() and until()
mwg:calculate-event-differentials.action: Use ZonedDateTime with IANA zones, calculate Duration with since() or until(), compare with relativeTo, and inspect sign for expiry.
mwg:calculate-event-differentials.blocker: Legacy Date tracks only epoch milliseconds, making calendar months, DST, and unit balancing error-prone without a concrete example. (quote: "The legacy `Date` object only tracks epoch milliseconds, making calendar-month arithmetic, Daylight Saving Time (DST) transitions, and unit balancing error-prone.")
mwg:calculate-event-differentials.outcome: Temporal provides calendar-aware differences and comparison; Safari needs a roughly 15 KB polyfill.
mwg:calculate-event-differentials.story: Durations no longer assume every day is 86,400,000 milliseconds.
mwg:calculate-event-differentials.unlock: Countdowns, trials, subscriptions, and SLA displays can calculate months and days directly without a date library. Safari needs a polyfill.
mwg:calculate-event-differentials.support: Temporal: Limited; Chrome/Edge 144 and Firefox 139, unsupported in Safari.

mwg:calculate-event-differentials:2.title: Format localized durations with Intl.DurationFormat
mwg:calculate-event-differentials:2.action: Use duration.toLocaleString() or Intl.DurationFormat with long, short, narrow, or digital style; reserve toString() for ISO machine output.
mwg:calculate-event-differentials:2.blocker: The guide rejects manually interpolated unit strings without giving a concrete failure.
mwg:calculate-event-differentials:2.outcome: Intl.DurationFormat produces locale-correct duration text and is Newly available.
mwg:calculate-event-differentials:2.story: Unit names, ordering, and separators come from locale data rather than string templates.
mwg:calculate-event-differentials:2.unlock: Elapsed time, remaining estimates, and media lengths can be localized in one call, including digital 1:30:00 formatting.

mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data.title: Use PlainDate and PlainTime for birthdays and alarms
mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data.action: Store calendar dates and wall-clock times in Temporal Plain types, and convert through Instant with an explicit zone only when Date is unavoidable.
mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data.blocker: Date represents an instant in the viewer's zone, so a saved 1990-01-01 can appear as 1989-12-31 west of UTC. (quote: "saving a date like `"1990-01-01"` can result in users west of UTC seeing `"1989-12-31"`")
mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data.outcome: Plain types preserve the same date everywhere; Safari needs a polyfill.
mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data.story: A calendar day is represented directly instead of choosing a midnight instant.
mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data.unlock: Birthdays, daily alarms, and store hours can synchronize across zones without shifting date or time. Safari needs a polyfill.

mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data:2.title: Use PlainYearMonth and PlainMonthDay for partial dates
mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data:2.action: Store month-only and day-only values in their matching Temporal types and choose explicit overflow behavior for recurrence.
mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data:2.blocker: Placeholder days for month-only values cause overflow bugs. (quote: "modeling partial dates (like a month-only card expiry) forces arbitrary placeholder days that cause overflow bugs.")
mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data:2.outcome: Partial-date types exclude fake days and recurrence can constrain or reject overflow; Safari needs a polyfill.
mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data:2.story: Card expiry and monthly recurrence no longer invent a day that later changes the month.
mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data:2.unlock: Subscriptions, anniversaries, and billing months can store exactly the precision they mean and declare end-of-month behavior. Safari needs a polyfill.

mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data:3.title: Identify time zones by IANA name, not fixed UTC offset
mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data:3.action: Use names such as America/New_York for time zones.
mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data:3.blocker: Offsets change with DST and legislation, so labels such as UTC-5 are wrong for part of the year. (quote: "Offsets change with daylight saving time and legislation, so labels like `"UTC-5"` become wrong for part of the year.")
mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data:3.outcome: IANA data applies DST and legal changes automatically; Safari needs the Temporal polyfill.
mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data:3.story: The geographic zone determines the offset instead of freezing one offset forever.

mwg:coordinate-global-events.title: Detect skipped and repeated DST times with ZonedDateTime disambiguation
mwg:coordinate-global-events.action: Use disambiguation reject to raise on invalid or ambiguous local times, compatible to choose automatically, and withTimeZone() for other cities.
mwg:coordinate-global-events.blocker: DST transitions skip or repeat hours, making cross-zone events difficult with legacy Date. (quote: "especially around Daylight Saving Time (DST) transitions when hours can be skipped or repeated.")
mwg:coordinate-global-events.outcome: Conflicts become detectable with an explicit resolution policy; PlainDateTime cannot handle DST and Safari needs a polyfill.
mwg:coordinate-global-events.story: Schedulers can reject nonexistent local times and show each attendee the corresponding time.
mwg:coordinate-global-events.unlock: International scheduling tools can warn immediately about nonexistent or duplicated times and list every attendee's local time. Safari needs a polyfill.

mwg:sort-high-precision-timestamps.title: Parse nanosecond timestamps with Temporal.Instant
mwg:sort-high-precision-timestamps.action: Parse server timestamps with Instant.from(), sort with Instant.compare(), and use since() and equals() for intervals and equality.
mwg:sort-high-precision-timestamps.blocker: Date silently truncates sub-millisecond digits, so distinct events collide and sort unstably. (quote: "parsing those strings with `new Date()` or `Date.parse()` silently truncates sub-millisecond digits, causing distinct events within the same millisecond to collide and sort in an unstable order.")
mwg:sort-high-precision-timestamps.outcome: Instant preserves nanoseconds for deterministic sorting; Safari needs a polyfill and browser-generated Now values remain reduced precision.
mwg:sort-high-precision-timestamps.story: Distributed trace events retain their real order instead of sharing one millisecond.
mwg:sort-high-precision-timestamps.unlock: Browser log viewers and telemetry timelines can sort server nanosecond timestamps and display microsecond or nanosecond intervals. Safari needs a polyfill.

mwg:sort-high-precision-timestamps:2.title: Keep intervals as Temporal.Duration instead of nanosecond Numbers
mwg:sort-high-precision-timestamps:2.action: Format Duration directly with toLocaleString() rather than total('nanoseconds').
mwg:sort-high-precision-timestamps:2.blocker: Nanosecond totals exceed Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER beyond roughly 104 days and silently lose precision. (quote: "`duration.total('nanoseconds')` returns a `Number`, which exceeds `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` for spans longer than ~104 days and silently loses precision.")
mwg:sort-high-precision-timestamps:2.outcome: Duration retains precision and unit structure; Safari needs a polyfill.
mwg:sort-high-precision-timestamps:2.story: Preserving timestamp precision is wasted if formatting converts the interval to an unsafe number.

mwg:support-global-calendar-systems.title: Use withCalendar() for Hebrew, Islamic, and Chinese calendar arithmetic
mwg:support-global-calendar-systems.action: Check supported calendars, convert with withCalendar(), compare in that calendar, and format with the matching Unicode locale extension.
mwg:support-global-calendar-systems.blocker: The guide says other calendars previously required complex libraries or manual calculations but gives no concrete failure. (quote: "Developers previously had to rely on complex third-party libraries or manual calculations to support these systems.")
mwg:support-global-calendar-systems.outcome: Temporal performs calendar arithmetic and formatting; Safari needs a polyfill and observation-based calendars remain approximations.
mwg:support-global-calendar-systems.story: Dates carry calendar identity through arithmetic, comparison, and formatting.
mwg:support-global-calendar-systems.unlock: Calendars and holiday reminders can support user-selected calendars and annual conversion without embedded calendar tables. Safari needs a polyfill.

mwg:support-global-calendar-systems:2.title: Use monthsInYear and monthCode instead of assuming twelve months
mwg:support-global-calendar-systems:2.action: Drive loops with monthsInYear and daysInMonth, identify months with monthCode, and compare month to monthsInYear for the final month.
mwg:support-global-calendar-systems:2.blocker: Lunisolar leap years can add a whole leap month, breaking fixed twelve-month loops and numeric cross-year comparisons. (quote: "DO NOT assume `inLeapYear === true` implies the year is only one day longer. In lunisolar calendars, it may add a full leap month.")
mwg:support-global-calendar-systems:2.outcome: Calendar invariants keep the same code correct across calendars; Safari needs a polyfill.
mwg:support-global-calendar-systems:2.story: Leap months no longer disappear from calendar components or shift numeric month lookups.

mwg:batch-analytics-events.title: Batch events with fetchLater() activateAfter
mwg:batch-analytics-events.action: Schedule fetchLater() with the current queue, cancel and reschedule when new events arrive, and clear the queue after activation.
mwg:batch-analytics-events.blocker: The guide claims a balance between timely updates and fewer beacons but gives no concrete old-approach failure.
mwg:batch-analytics-events.outcome: Supporting browsers batch the window and guarantee sending on page exit; Firefox and Safari use a visibilitychange polyfill.
mwg:batch-analytics-events.story: Browser scheduling handles both a quiet time window and early page exit.
mwg:batch-analytics-events.unlock: Lightweight analytics, drafts, and reading progress can batch briefly without losing data on tab close. Native support is Chromium-only.
mwg:batch-analytics-events.support: fetchLater: Limited; Chrome/Edge 135, unsupported in Firefox and Safari.

mwg:batch-analytics-events:2.title: Limit fetchLater() batch size and catch quota errors
mwg:batch-analytics-events:2.action: Cap the queue, wrap scheduling in try/catch, and avoid ReadableStream bodies.
mwg:batch-analytics-events:2.blocker: Oversized batches exceed the roughly 64 KB per-origin quota and throw. (quote: "DO check to ensure you do not batch too many events together and exceed the `fetchLater()` quota (currently roughly 64KB per origin).")
mwg:batch-analytics-events:2.outcome: Limits and error handling keep quota failures from stopping the pipeline.
mwg:batch-analytics-events:2.story: An unbounded queue can otherwise prevent every later event from being scheduled.

mwg:form-fields-automatically-fit-conten.title: Cancel flex and grid stretching for content-sized fields
mwg:form-fields-automatically-fit-conten.action: Set align-self:start or justify-self:start on field-sizing controls inside grid and flex layouts.
mwg:form-fields-automatically-fit-conten.blocker: Grid and flex layouts implicitly stretch children, preventing fields from shrinking to their content. (quote: "Grid and Flexbox layouts often implicitly stretch their children to fill available space.")
mwg:form-fields-automatically-fit-conten.outcome: Overriding stretch lets fields shrink to content; field-sizing is Newly.
mwg:form-fields-automatically-fit-conten.story: The container alignment default can defeat auto-sizing even after explicit widths are reset.

mwg:autofill-highlight-inputs:4.title: Preserve focus shadows and caret color when overriding autofill colors
mwg:autofill-highlight-inputs:4.action: Prefer the browser colors; otherwise use inset shadow, -webkit-text-fill-color, and caret-color, repeating existing focus shadows in the same declaration.
mwg:autofill-highlight-inputs:4.blocker: UA !important colors require workarounds, and an inset-shadow workaround replaces existing box-shadow focus rings. (quote: "All browsers also set `background-color`, `background-image`, and `color` on autofilled fields with `!important` in their user agent stylesheets, so overriding them relies on workarounds.")
mwg:autofill-highlight-inputs:4.outcome: Colors can change without losing focus indication; :autofill remains Limited.
mwg:autofill-highlight-inputs:4.story: The brand background and focus ring compete for the same box-shadow property.

mwg:animated-select-picker:5.title: Give base-select an explicit width
mwg:animated-select-picker:5.action: Set a fixed width or flex/grid constraints after enabling appearance: base-select.
mwg:animated-select-picker:5.blocker: base-select removes longest-option sizing, so selected content changes width and shifts layout. (quote: "Setting `appearance: base-select` removes the default browser behavior of sizing the select based on its longest option width. You may need to set a fixed width or use flex/grid constraints to prevent layout shifts.")
mwg:animated-select-picker:5.outcome: An explicit width keeps neighboring content stationary.
mwg:animated-select-picker:5.story: Customizable select no longer reserves width for the longest option.

mwg:custom-select-picker-layouts:4.title: Give base-select an explicit width
mwg:custom-select-picker-layouts:4.action: Set a fixed width or flex/grid constraints after enabling appearance: base-select.
mwg:custom-select-picker-layouts:4.blocker: base-select removes longest-option sizing, so selected content changes width and shifts layout. (quote: "Setting `appearance: base-select` removes the default browser behavior of sizing the select based on its longest option width. You may need to set a fixed width or use flex/grid constraints to prevent layout shifts.")
mwg:custom-select-picker-layouts:4.outcome: An explicit width keeps neighboring content stationary.
mwg:custom-select-picker-layouts:4.story: Customizable select no longer reserves width for the longest option.

mwg:animated-select-picker:4.title: Disable picker and icon animation under reduced motion
mwg:animated-select-picker:4.action: Disable picker and picker-icon transitions inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
mwg:animated-select-picker:4.blocker: Menu scaling, fading, and icon rotation can affect people with motion sickness. (quote: "Always wrap animation constraints in a `prefers-reduced-motion` media query to ensure accessible environments for those affected by motion sickness.")
mwg:animated-select-picker:4.outcome: The menu opens directly without rotation for users requesting reduced motion.
mwg:animated-select-picker:4.story: System motion preferences must also apply to decorative select animation.

mwg:custom-select-picker-layouts:5.title: Add geometric left/right navigation while preserving linear up/down navigation
mwg:custom-select-picker-layouts:5.action: Handle Left and Right with getBoundingClientRect(), retain sequential Up and Down, and do not apply grid role to the picker.
mwg:custom-select-picker-layouts:5.blocker: Native select only handles linear Up/Down, so Left/Right do nothing; removing sequential navigation can hide options from screen-reader users. (quote: "A native `<select>` only handles linear Up/Down arrow navigation, so Left/Right do nothing in the open picker and Up/Down still navigate items sequentially, regardless of rows and columns.")
mwg:custom-select-picker-layouts:5.outcome: Arrow keys follow the visual grid while every option remains sequentially reachable.
mwg:custom-select-picker-layouts:5.story: Actual geometry handles irregular grids and RTL better than parsing CSS track strings.

mwg:style-parent-with-has:4.title: Announce errors through one delayed polite live region
mwg:style-parent-with-has:4.action: Send field errors to one page-level polite live region after a short delay, and focus the first invalid field after failed submission.
mwg:style-parent-with-has:4.blocker: A live region that is merely shown rather than changed is not announced reliably, and simultaneous messages can talk over the next field. (quote: "a live region that is shown, rather than changed, isn't announced reliably.")
mwg:style-parent-with-has:4.outcome: Changing shared-region text makes the error audible without competing with focus announcements.
mwg:style-parent-with-has:4.story: The live region must exist from page load and receive a text update, not merely become visible.

mwg:required-field-feedback:4.title: Announce errors through one delayed polite live region
mwg:required-field-feedback:4.action: Send field errors to one page-level polite live region after a short delay, and focus the first invalid field after failed submission.
mwg:required-field-feedback:4.blocker: A live region that is merely shown rather than changed is not announced reliably, and simultaneous messages can talk over the next field. (quote: "a live region that is shown, rather than changed, isn't announced reliably.")
mwg:required-field-feedback:4.outcome: Changing shared-region text makes the error audible without competing with focus announcements.
mwg:required-field-feedback:4.story: The live region must exist from page load and receive a text update, not merely become visible.

mwg:required-field-feedback:5.title: Hide required-field asterisks from assistive technology
mwg:required-field-feedback:5.action: Wrap visual asterisks in aria-hidden spans, explain the convention once, and retain the required attribute.
mwg:required-field-feedback:5.blocker: required already announces the state, so an exposed asterisk adds redundant speech. (quote: "wrap it in `*`, because the `required` attribute already makes screen readers announce "required".")
mwg:required-field-feedback:5.outcome: Sighted users keep the asterisk while screen readers announce required once.
mwg:required-field-feedback:5.story: Visual decoration should not duplicate a programmatic state.

mwg:required-field-feedback:6.title: Keep submit enabled so the browser reveals required errors
mwg:required-field-feedback:6.action: Leave submit enabled before validity; activation triggers :user-invalid and focuses the first invalid field.
mwg:required-field-feedback:6.blocker: A disabled submit prevents users from requesting validation and receiving error and focus guidance. (quote: "Unlike `disabled` buttons, keep your submit button enabled. If the user clicks it, the browser will automatically trigger `:user-invalid` on all empty required fields and focus the first one.")
mwg:required-field-feedback:6.outcome: Submission reveals missing fields and focuses the first error.
mwg:required-field-feedback:6.story: A disabled button says only that submission is unavailable, not what needs fixing.

mwg:autofill-payment-form:4.title: Use text and numeric inputmode for card numbers
mwg:autofill-payment-form:4.action: Use type="text", inputmode="numeric", and cc-number autocomplete, allowing spaces and appropriate lengths.
mwg:autofill-payment-form:4.blocker: Number inputs add spinners and strip leading zeros. (quote: "DO NOT use type="number" — it adds increment/decrement controls and strips leading zeros")
mwg:autofill-payment-form:4.outcome: Mobile retains a numeric keyboard while the card number remains an exact string.
mwg:autofill-payment-form:4.story: A card number is an identifier, not a quantity.

mwg:autofill-payment-form:5.title: Place payment format hints above the input
mwg:autofill-payment-form:5.action: Put persistent hints above fields and connect them with aria-describedby; use placeholder only as an extra cue.
mwg:autofill-payment-form:5.blocker: Mobile keyboards and autofill popovers cover hints below inputs, and placeholder disappears during entry. (quote: "Hints that sit below an input are easily hidden by the mobile keyboard or by the autofill popover at the moment the user needs them.")
mwg:autofill-payment-form:5.outcome: The format remains visible and programmatically associated while editing.
mwg:autofill-payment-form:5.story: Moving the hint avoids both overlays.

mwg:autofill-payment-form:6.title: Do not mask the card security code
mwg:autofill-payment-form:6.action: Use type="text", numeric inputmode, and cc-csc autocomplete instead of type="password".
mwg:autofill-payment-form:6.blocker: Users cannot check masked digits, so a typo appears only after payment is declined. (quote: "Users can't check a masked three- or four-digit code for typos, so a mistyped digit isn't caught until the payment is declined")
mwg:autofill-payment-form:6.outcome: Users can verify the code before submitting.
mwg:autofill-payment-form:6.story: Masking a code printed on the card adds little protection but removes a useful check.

mwg:autofill-payment-form:7.title: Use one field for card and phone numbers
mwg:autofill-payment-form:7.action: Keep each number in one input and create grouped visuals with styling rather than multiple fields.
mwg:autofill-payment-form:7.blocker: Splitting numbers prevents browser autofill and complicates entry and validation. (quote: "For payment card and phone numbers use a single input: don't split the number into parts. That makes it easier for users to enter data, makes validation simpler, and enables browsers to autofill.")
mwg:autofill-payment-form:7.outcome: The browser fills and validates the complete value in one field.
mwg:autofill-payment-form:7.story: The visual grouping no longer determines the data-entry structure.

mwg:autofill-payment-form:8.title: Allow varied card lengths and spaces in patterns
mwg:autofill-payment-form:8.action: Accept valid issuer lengths and spaces, removing spaces before processing.
mwg:autofill-payment-form:8.blocker: Rigid patterns reject valid cards and the grouped spaces printed on physical cards. (quote: "Allow users to include spaces when they're entering a new payment card number, since this is how numbers are displayed on physical cards.")
mwg:autofill-payment-form:8.outcome: Valid lengths and spaces pass frontend validation while processing still receives clean digits.
mwg:autofill-payment-form:8.story: Users should not have to retype the format shown on their card.

mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:4.title: Allow Unicode letters in name validation
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:4.action: Use Unicode-aware matching and secure Unicode handling on the backend.
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:4.blocker: Latin-only validation excludes users whose names or addresses use other writing systems. (quote: "Latin-only excludes users with names or addresses that include characters that aren't in the Latin alphabet.")
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:4.outcome: Names in non-Latin scripts pass validation.
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:4.story: Names are international data, not English identifiers.

mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:5.title: Use a real form instead of div-based JavaScript-only submission
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:5.action: Put credentials in a form with a submit button and preserve native submission before enhancing with JavaScript.
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:5.blocker: JavaScript-only submission leaves the flow unusable when scripts fail and loses native accessibility behavior. (quote: "can still work even if JavaScript fails.")
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:5.outcome: Native form submission remains available as a fallback.
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:5.story: Visible fields are useless if script failure removes their only submission path.

mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:6.title: Do not ask for email or password twice
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:6.action: Request each value once and provide password visibility, confirmation, or reset paths instead of duplicate fields.
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:6.blocker: Repeated entry adds work for everyone and increases abandonment, especially with autofill and generated passwords. (quote: "causes extra work for all users, and increases abandonment rates.")
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:6.outcome: The flow loses a redundant round of typing and comparison.
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:6.story: Duplicate fields defeat the automation supplied by password managers.

mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:7.title: Keep credentials and submit above the mobile keyboard
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:7.action: Place only identifier, password, and the primary button near the top, moving secondary content below.
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:7.blocker: Mobile keyboards can cover the form or button, and users may give up before understanding why. (quote: "mobile keyboards may cover your form or, worse, partially obstruct the Sign in button. Users may give up before realizing what has happened.")
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:7.outcome: Core input and submission stay visible without dismissing the keyboard.
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:7.story: A concise first screen prevents the keyboard from hiding the next action.

mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:8.title: Allow pasting into password fields
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:8.action: Do not block paste events; support password managers and visible-password controls.
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:8.blocker: Blocking paste encourages memorable, easier-to-compromise passwords and does not remove clipboard risk. (quote: "Disallowing password pasting annoys users, encourages passwords that are memorable (and therefore may be easier to compromise)")
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:8.outcome: Long unique passwords can be pasted or filled without being simplified for manual typing.
mwg:autofill-sign-in-form:8.story: The apparent security measure mainly penalizes password-manager users.

mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:4.title: Allow Unicode letters in name validation
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:4.action: Use Unicode-aware matching and secure Unicode handling on the backend.
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:4.blocker: Latin-only validation excludes users whose names or addresses use other writing systems. (quote: "Latin-only excludes users with names or addresses that include characters that aren't in the Latin alphabet.")
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:4.outcome: Names in non-Latin scripts pass validation.
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:4.story: Names are international data, not English identifiers.

mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:5.title: Use a real form instead of div-based JavaScript-only submission
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:5.action: Put credentials in a form with a submit button and preserve native submission before enhancing with JavaScript.
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:5.blocker: JavaScript-only submission leaves the flow unusable when scripts fail and loses native accessibility behavior. (quote: "can still work even if JavaScript fails.")
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:5.outcome: Native form submission remains available as a fallback.
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:5.story: Visible fields are useless if script failure removes their only submission path.

mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:6.title: Do not ask for email or password twice
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:6.action: Request each value once and provide password visibility, confirmation, or reset paths instead of duplicate fields.
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:6.blocker: Repeated entry adds work for everyone and increases abandonment, especially with autofill and generated passwords. (quote: "causes extra work for all users, and increases abandonment rates.")
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:6.outcome: The flow loses a redundant round of typing and comparison.
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:6.story: Duplicate fields defeat the automation supplied by password managers.

mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:7.title: Keep credentials and submit above the mobile keyboard
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:7.action: Place only identifier, password, and the primary button near the top, moving secondary content below.
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:7.blocker: Mobile keyboards can cover the form or button, and users may give up before understanding why. (quote: "mobile keyboards may cover your form or, worse, partially obstruct the Sign up button. Users may give up before realizing what has happened.")
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:7.outcome: Core input and submission stay visible without dismissing the keyboard.
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:7.story: A concise first screen prevents the keyboard from hiding the next action.

mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:8.title: Allow pasting into password fields
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:8.action: Do not block paste events; support password managers and visible-password controls.
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:8.blocker: Blocking paste encourages memorable, easier-to-compromise passwords and does not remove clipboard risk. (quote: "Disallowing password pasting annoys users, encourages passwords that are memorable (and therefore may be easier to compromise)")
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:8.outcome: Long unique passwords can be pasted or filled without being simplified for manual typing.
mwg:autofill-sign-up-form:8.story: The apparent security measure mainly penalizes password-manager users.

mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dial.title: Lock the page behind a modal with `overscroll-behavior: contain` instead of changing `<body>` overflow
mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dial.action: Set `overscroll-behavior: contain` on `dialog:modal`; set `overflow: hidden` on `dialog::backdrop` to make it a non-scrollable scroll container, then `overscroll-behavior: contain` on it too
mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dial.blocker: `showModal()` blocks clicks and focus but not scrolling: scrolling over the backdrop or past the end of the dialog scrolls the page; the old fix of `overflow: hidden` or `position: fixed` on `<html>`/`<body>` removes the scrollbar, shifts layout and jumps the scroll position (quote: "Mutating root overflow removes the page scrollbar (causing horizontal layout shift), can reset or jump the page scroll position, and can break `position: sticky` elements")
mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dial.outcome: Supporting browsers fully stop background scrolling both over the backdrop and inside the dialog; Safari does not yet apply overscroll-behavior to non-scrollable containers, so it only contains scrolling when the dialog content overflows, while `showModal()` still makes the page inert (official claim)
mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dial.story: With a modal open, one swipe on the dimmed backdrop quietly scrolled the article behind it; the body-lock trick made the whole page jump sideways and broke sticky headers. Two CSS declarations now keep scrolling inside the dialog; Safari is the remaining gap.
mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dial.unlock: Locking background scroll used to mean touching the root element and paying with layout jumps → lightboxes, confirmations, and full-screen settings panels can lock the background in pure CSS, and the page stays put with sticky intact on close. Safari only when the dialog content overflows
mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dial.support: overscroll-behavior (on non-scrollable scroll containers): Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 144, Edge 144, Firefox 150. Unsupported in: Safari

mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dial.title: Don't feature-detect overscroll support on non-scrollable containers with `@supports`
mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dial.action: Treat dialog scroll containment as progressive enhancement; do not branch on `@supports (overscroll-behavior: contain)` or `CSS.supports()`
mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dial.blocker: Every modern browser recognises the syntax and returns true, even if it only enforces the property when content overflows (quote: "All modern browsers support the `overscroll-behavior: contain` property syntax and return `true`, even if they only enforce it when content overflows.")
mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dial.outcome: Writing it unconditionally gives full containment where supported and containment on overflow elsewhere (official claim)
mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dial.story: A detection branch meant to add a Safari fallback also passed in Safari, so the fallback never ran. The behaviour cannot be detected; write it and accept the difference.

mwg:same-document-transitions.title: Use `startViewTransition()` with a shared `view-transition-name` so a thumbnail grows into the detail-page hero
mwg:same-document-transitions.action: Wrap SPA view changes in `document.startViewTransition()`; give the list item and the detail hero the same `view-transition-name` (unique names in the list applied dynamically to the detail page, or the reverse with only the selected item named)
mwg:same-document-transitions.blocker: Clicking from list to detail makes the thumbnail vanish and a larger image appear elsewhere instantly, so users lose track of how the two relate (quote: "the thumbnail disappears and a new, larger image appears instantly elsewhere on the screen. This lack of continuity makes it harder for users to track relationships between elements.")
mwg:same-document-transitions.outcome: The browser computes position, size and style differences and morphs smoothly; View Transitions are Newly available, and unsupported browsers update the DOM without animation (official claim)
mwg:same-document-transitions.story: Clicking into a product made the screen jump and the eye had to find the image again. Wrapping the update in a transition and naming both ends lets the image fly from where it was to where it goes. Older browsers just switch instantly.
mwg:same-document-transitions.unlock: List-to-detail continuity used to need a FLIP animation library → photo albums, product catalogues and contact lists can morph the clicked card into the detail view in a few lines of JS, with plain switching where unsupported

mwg:same-document-transitions:2.title: Each `view-transition-name` may belong to only one element before and after; clear temporary names afterwards
mwg:same-document-transitions:2.action: Ensure each name maps to one element before and after the transition; remove names added via `.selected` after `transition.finished`
mwg:same-document-transitions:2.blocker: With two or more elements sharing a name, the DOM updates immediately with no transition (quote: "If there are 2 or more elements with a given `view-transition-name`, the DOM will be updated to the new state immediately, without a transition.")
mwg:same-document-transitions:2.outcome: Unique names cleaned up after each run keep the next navigation from failing (official claim)
mwg:same-document-transitions:2.story: The first click animated; back on the list, clicking another card did nothing — the name left on the previous item collided with the new one.

mwg:same-document-transitions:3.title: Transitions don't manage focus: move it to the new heading yourself
mwg:same-document-transitions:3.action: After the DOM update or when `transition.finished` resolves, focus the new view's heading or container (`tabindex="-1"`), including in the no-transition branch
mwg:same-document-transitions:3.blocker: If focus stays on an element hidden or removed during the transition, it is abandoned and keyboard and AT users lose context (quote: "If focus remains on an element that is hidden or removed during the transition, focus is abandoned, leaving keyboard and assistive technology users without context.")
mwg:same-document-transitions:3.outcome: Focus routed to the new heading announces the new context and keeps the tab order connected (official claim)
mwg:same-document-transitions:3.story: Pressing a thumbnail by keyboard morphed beautifully into the detail page, but focus fell back to the top and the next Tab started over.

mwg:same-document-transitions:4.title: Use `fit-content` on transitioning text so snapshots don't stretch
mwg:same-document-transitions:4.action: Set `width: fit-content` on the transitioning text in both views; for elements that change aspect ratio set `height: 100%` on `::view-transition-old/new()` and use `object-fit` if needed
mwg:same-document-transitions:4.blocker: By default the old and new snapshots cross-fade inside a group that stretches to fit both, distorting them (quote: "By default, the browser cross-fades the old and new snapshots within a group that stretches to fit both.")
mwg:same-document-transitions:4.outcome: With widths fitted to content, the element's aspect ratio stays stable during the transition (official claim)
mwg:same-document-transitions:4.story: The title flying from list to detail got squashed and then stretched. A snapshot is an image; it takes whatever width its group has.

mwg:scoped-component-transitions.title: Use `element.startViewTransition()` to keep a transition inside a component instead of covering the page
mwg:scoped-component-transitions.action: Call `element.startViewTransition()` on the component root, name children with `view-transition-name: match-element`, and add `view-transition-scope: all` to repeated component containers so names don't leak
mwg:scoped-component-transitions.blocker: `document.startViewTransition()` attaches the overlay to `:root`, so during the transition the page can't be clicked, transitions can't run concurrently, and fixed headers and open popovers are covered (quote: "blocks pointer events on the rest of the page, prevents concurrent transitions, and obscures `position: fixed` headers or open `[popover]` elements")
mwg:scoped-component-transitions.outcome: In supporting browsers the overlay covers only the component, the rest of the page stays interactive and several components can transition at once; Chrome/Edge 147 only, and elsewhere the guide recommends updating without animation since falling back to a document transition brings the problems back (official claim)
mwg:scoped-component-transitions.story: While a sidebar list was animating a reorder, the header buttons couldn't be clicked and an open menu was hidden under the transition. Scoping it to the component leaves the rest of the page alone — but only Chromium can do it for now.
mwg:scoped-component-transitions.unlock: A small component's animation used to freeze the whole page → dashboard cards can each animate sorting, adding and removing at the same time while the header and floating toolbars stay clickable. Chromium only for now
mwg:scoped-component-transitions.support: Element-scoped view transitions: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 147, Edge 147. Unsupported in: Firefox, Safari (View transitions themselves are Newly)

mwg:scoped-component-transitions:2.title: `match-element` needs existing nodes moved, not rebuilt with `innerHTML`
mwg:scoped-component-transitions:2.action: With `view-transition-name: match-element`, reorder or remove by moving and removing existing DOM nodes
mwg:scoped-component-transitions:2.blocker: `match-element` pairs by DOM node identity, so recreated nodes cannot match the old ones (quote: "Preserve and move existing DOM nodes (rather than recreating them with `innerHTML`) when using `view-transition-name: match-element`, as `match-element` tracks DOM node identity.")
mwg:scoped-component-transitions:2.outcome: Moving existing nodes gives every item an automatic name and its own morph (official claim)
mwg:scoped-component-transitions:2.story: After sorting, the whole list was re-rendered; items in the transition couldn't find their predecessors and only cross-faded.

mwg:scoped-component-transitions:3.title: Catch the `ready` rejection when a component re-triggers transitions rapidly
mwg:scoped-component-transitions:3.blocker: Calling it again on the same element skips the active transition and rejects `ready`, which becomes an unhandled promise rejection if not caught (quote: "Re-triggering startViewTransition() on the same element skips the active transition and rejects `ready`.")
mwg:scoped-component-transitions:3.outcome: Rapid clicks just skip the old transition without errors (official claim)
mwg:scoped-component-transitions:3.story: A user clicked "Sort" repeatedly and the console filled with unhandled rejections.

mwg:scoped-component-transitions:4.title: Don't set `view-transition-name: none` on a scope element that clips overflow
mwg:scoped-component-transitions:4.action: Let the scope keep its default self-participation (`view-transition-name: root`) so `::view-transition-group-children(root)` automatically applies `overflow: clip`
mwg:scoped-component-transitions:4.blocker: Opting out of self-participation disables automatic overflow clipping, so transitioning children spill outside the component (quote: "opting out of self-participation disables automatic overflow clipping.")
mwg:scoped-component-transitions:4.outcome: With the default kept, children stay clipped to the component and the component's own size change animates too (official claim)
mwg:scoped-component-transitions:4.story: During a reorder, items in a scrollable card flew outside the card and over the neighbouring content.

mwg:scoped-component-transitions:5.title: When an outer transition must move the component, wrap it in a named wrapper and set the inner scope to `view-transition-scope: all`
mwg:scoped-component-transitions:5.action: Wrap the scope element in a wrapper with its own `view-transition-name` and add `view-transition-scope: all` to the scope; or, if the outer transition captures children, use nested transition groups and re-apply `overflow: clip` manually
mwg:scoped-component-transitions:5.blocker: An outer transition started from a parent or the document captures and animates the scope element and everything inside it (quote: "the outer transition will capture and animate the scope element and everything inside it.")
mwg:scoped-component-transitions:5.outcome: The outer transition animates only the wrapper and the inner transition can finish (official claim)
mwg:scoped-component-transitions:5.story: As soon as a page-level transition began, the small transition running inside a card was interrupted and its items were grabbed by the outer one.

mwg:scroll-completion-effects.title: `await scrollIntoView()` until scrolling really stops instead of guessing with `setTimeout`
mwg:scroll-completion-effects.action: Make the handler `async` and `await element.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth' })` (or `scrollTo()`, `scrollBy()`), then add the highlight, start the animation or move focus
mwg:scroll-completion-effects.blocker: Guessing scroll duration with `setTimeout()` fires too early on long scrolls and too late on short ones; a hand-wrapped `scrollend` promise never resolves when the target is already in view (quote: "fires too early on long scrolls and too late on short ones"; "`scrollend` does not fire when the target is already in view and no scrolling occurs")
mwg:scroll-completion-effects.outcome: In supporting browsers the promise resolves when scrolling ends, or immediately if no scroll is needed; Chrome/Edge 150 only, and elsewhere `await` continues immediately, so accuracy still needs the old `scrollend` plus timeout approach (official claim)
mwg:scroll-completion-effects.story: Clicking a table-of-contents entry should scroll and then flash a highlight, but the flash finished while the section was still off-screen. With the scroll methods returning promises the timing needs no guessing — though Firefox and Safari still need the hand-built version.
mwg:scroll-completion-effects.unlock: "Scroll there, then act" used to mean guessing or wiring scrollend → guided tours, line-by-line code walkthroughs and map lists can `await` each scroll and highlight in straight-line code. Chromium only for now
mwg:scroll-completion-effects.support: Scroll method promises: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 150, Edge 150. Unsupported in: Firefox, Safari

mwg:scroll-completion-effects:2.title: Interrupted smooth scrolls also resolve: use an incrementing ID to drop stale follow-ups
mwg:scroll-completion-effects:2.action: Increment an operation ID before each scroll and return early after `await` if it is no longer the latest
mwg:scroll-completion-effects:2.blocker: When a new scroll interrupts a smooth scroll, the browser resolves rather than rejects all pending promises, so the old follow-up still runs (quote: "the browser aborts the ongoing smooth scroll and **resolves** (does not reject) all pending scroll promises on that container.")
mwg:scroll-completion-effects:2.outcome: Only the latest scroll's effect runs (official claim)
mwg:scroll-completion-effects:2.story: A user clicked three sections quickly and all three flashed their highlight.

mwg:scroll-completion-effects:3.title: Pass `{ preventScroll: true }` when focusing after a scroll
mwg:scroll-completion-effects:3.action: After awaiting the scroll, call `focus({ preventScroll: true })`
mwg:scroll-completion-effects:3.blocker: `focus()` scrolls again by default, fighting the scroll that just finished (quote: "so the browser does not jump or scroll a second time.")
mwg:scroll-completion-effects:3.outcome: Focus moves without a second jump (official claim)
mwg:scroll-completion-effects:3.story: The smooth scroll centred the section, then focusing the heading jerked it to the top of the screen.
mwg:scroll-completion-effects:3.support: focus() preventScroll: no support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:scroll-completion-effects:4.title: Chrome resolves too early when scrolling the root scroller; don't wrap content in a scroll container to work around it
mwg:scroll-completion-effects:4.action: Know the bug exists: `scrollIntoView()` on nested scroll containers works, but don't wrap content in an `overflow-y: auto` div as a workaround
mwg:scroll-completion-effects:4.blocker: When the document's root scroller is scrolling, Chrome resolves the `scrollIntoView()` promise too early (quote: "Chrome has a bug where the `Promise` returned by `scrollIntoView()` resolves too early when it is the document's root scroller that is scrolling.")
mwg:scroll-completion-effects:4.outcome: The guide gives no fix beyond not wrapping, so page-level effects may still fire early (official claim)
mwg:scroll-completion-effects:4.story: The same code timed perfectly inside a sidebar list flashed early when used on the whole page.

mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects.title: Build entry and exit effects with `view()` and `animation-range: entry, exit`
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects.action: Write separate `@keyframes` for entry (fill `backwards`) and exit (fill `forwards`), bind them with `animation-timeline: view()` to the element's own visibility, and limit them with `animation-range: entry, exit`; or use range selectors like `entry 0%` and `exit 100%` in one `@keyframes`
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects.blocker: The guide doesn't say what breaks in the old approach; it only says the fallback is IntersectionObserver and native is more performant (quote: "In browsers with built-in support for scroll-driven animations, ALWAYS use the native CSS implementation as those are more performant.")
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects.outcome: Pure CSS drives entry and exit by scroll position; scroll-driven animations are Newly available and decorative effects may skip a fallback (official claim)
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects.story: Cards that grow as they slide in and shrink as they leave used to need an observer per element and ratio maths. Now one set of keyframes on a view timeline moves exactly as much as you scroll.
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects.unlock: Entry and exit effects used to need IntersectionObserver ratios per element → horizontal galleries, timelines and product rows can scale and fade each item as it enters and leaves, rewinding automatically when scrolled back

mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects:2.title: `@supports` must also check `animation-range: entry`
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects:2.action: Write the check as `@supports ((animation-timeline: view()) and (animation-range: entry))`
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects:2.blocker: Checking only `animation-timeline` lets partially supporting browsers through (quote: "The `(animation-range: entry)` check **MUST** be included here, to filter out browsers with only partial support.")
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects:2.outcome: Partially supporting browsers are filtered out and take the fallback or no effect (official claim)
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects:2.story: Detection passed, but in some browsers the effect ran in the wrong range.

mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects:3.title: Put `animation-timeline` and `animation-range` after the `animation` shorthand
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects:3.action: Write the `animation` shorthand first, then `animation-timeline` and `animation-range`
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects:3.blocker: A shorthand written later resets the timeline and range (quote: "declare `animation-timeline` and `animation-range` *after* it to prevent the shorthand from resetting them.")
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects:3.outcome: In the right order the timeline and range are kept (official claim)
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects:3.story: The animation played once on page load, unrelated to scrolling.

mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects:4.title: In a single keyframes rule, spell out the resting state across the middle
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects:4.action: Set the resting value (e.g. `scale: 1`) at `entry 100%, exit 0%` together, with `animation-fill-mode: both`
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects:4.blocker: Without the middle, the element interpolates straight from `entry 0%` to `exit 100%` (quote: "Explicitly set the resting state across the middle (`contain`) phase so the element doesn't interpolate straight from entry 0% to exit 100%")
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects:4.outcome: The element stays at its normal size while fully in view (official claim)
mwg:scroll-entry-exit-effects:4.story: Cards started shrinking the moment they entered, never resting at normal size.

mwg:scroll-snap-realtime-feedback.title: Use `scrollsnapchanging` to mark the pending snap target before the finger lifts
mwg:scroll-snap-realtime-feedback.action: Listen for `scrollsnapchanging` on the scroll container and use `event.snapTargetInline` (or `snapTargetBlock`) to add a `pending` style to the matching thumbnail; listen for `scrollsnapchange` to make it `active` and update `aria-current` once it actually snaps
mwg:scroll-snap-realtime-feedback.blocker: Traditional scroll snap only gives feedback after the gesture completes and the element settles (quote: "Traditional scroll snap only provides feedback *after* the scroll gesture completes and the element settles.")
mwg:scroll-snap-realtime-feedback.outcome: Supporting browsers can highlight the item about to settle while dragging; Chrome/Edge 129 only, and other browsers must compute the closest item with `scroll` plus `requestAnimationFrame` or the linked UI desynchronises from the content (official claim)
mwg:scroll-snap-realtime-feedback.story: Swiping the gallery, the thumbnail strip only switched its highlight after the swipe settled; mid-drag you couldn't tell where it would land. The native event announces "about to stop here" early, but only Chromium provides it.
mwg:scroll-snap-realtime-feedback.unlock: Snap feedback used to wait until settling → wheel-style pickers (date, time, quantity) and gallery thumbnail strips can preview the result mid-drag, lighting up like a physical dial. Chromium only for now
mwg:scroll-snap-realtime-feedback.support: Scroll snap events: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 129, Edge 129. Unsupported in: Firefox, Safari (scroll snap itself is Widely)

mwg:scroll-snap-realtime-feedback:2.title: Sync the initial state yourself when the scroll position is restored on load
mwg:scroll-snap-realtime-feedback:2.action: On page load (`load` or `readyState === 'complete'`), run one geometric check to find the item closest to centre and mark it active
mwg:scroll-snap-realtime-feedback:2.blocker: When the browser restores the scroll position via history or an anchor, neither `scrollsnapchange` nor `scroll` fires (quote: "Neither `scrollsnapchange` nor `scroll` events will fire automatically.")
mwg:scroll-snap-realtime-feedback:2.outcome: The one-off check aligns the initial highlight with the actual position (official claim)
mwg:scroll-snap-realtime-feedback:2.story: Going back to the gallery, the view sat on the fifth photo while the thumbnail strip still highlighted the first.

mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync.title: Use `scrollsnapchange` to sync the table-of-contents highlight when scrolling settles on a new section
mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync.action: Set `scroll-snap-type` on the container and `scroll-snap-align: start` on section headings, listen for `scrollsnapchange`, and update the active sidebar link from `event.snapTargetBlock`
mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync.blocker: The guide only says this used to need complex scroll listeners, manual offset maths and IntersectionObserver, not when those break (quote: "traditionally required complex scroll event listeners, manual calculations of scroll offsets, and intersection observers.")
mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync.outcome: Supporting browsers fire once when scrolling settles on a new snap target; Chrome/Edge 129 only, other browsers fall back to IntersectionObserver, which fires during the scroll rather than after it settles (official claim)
mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync.story: A long article with a sidebar TOC should light up whichever section you are reading; you used to compute that yourself. Snap events hand you "where it stopped", but cross-browser you still keep an observer version.
mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync.unlock: "Which section are we on?" used to need offset maths → slide-style documents, chaptered help pages and vertical short-video feeds can sync page numbers, TOCs or playback when scrolling stops. Chromium only for now
mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync.support: Scroll snap events: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 129, Edge 129. Unsupported in: Firefox, Safari

mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync:2.title: Snap events only sync visuals; expose the active state with `aria-current`
mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync:2.action: Set `aria-current="true"` or `"location"` on the active TOC link and wrap the TOC in a named `<nav>`
mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync:2.blocker: Scroll snap events sync the screen but don't expose that state programmatically (quote: "it does not automatically expose that information programmatically.")
mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync:2.outcome: The active state is reflected in the accessibility tree (official claim)
mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync:2.story: Visually the TOC highlighted section three; a screen reader user heard every link the same and couldn't tell where they were.
mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync:2.support: aria-current: no support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync:3.title: Be careful with `mandatory` snapping when sections are taller than the screen
mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync:3.action: Use `scroll-snap-type: y proximity` for section snapping in long articles rather than `mandatory`
mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync:3.blocker: `mandatory` can make content between snap points that is taller than the screen unreachable (quote: "it can cause content in-between snap-points to become inaccessible when longer than the screen.")
mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync:3.outcome: `proximity` only snaps near snap points, so content in between scrolls freely (official claim)
mwg:scroll-snap-state-sync:3.story: A section longer than the screen kept yanking you to the next heading; the second half was never visible.

mwg:scroll-target-on-load.title: Use `scroll-initial-target: nearest` so a list opens on a chosen item
mwg:scroll-target-on-load.action: Set `scroll-initial-target: nearest` on the child that should be visible first (today in a calendar, a specific photo in a gallery, a featured item in a feed)
mwg:scroll-target-on-load.blocker: This used to be done with `scrollIntoView()` or a `#item-id` fragment; the guide only says both have limitations and are tricky, not when they break (quote: "both of which have limitations and are tricky to implement.")
mwg:scroll-target-on-load.outcome: Supporting browsers bring the target into view during layout; Chrome/Edge 133 only, other browsers still need `scrollIntoView({ behavior: "instant" })` after `DOMContentLoaded` (official claim)
mwg:scroll-target-on-load.story: A calendar should open on today, not January 1st. The property lets CSS declare the starting position without waiting for script; Firefox and Safari still need the script.
mwg:scroll-target-on-load.unlock: Middle-start scrolling used to wait for JS → calendars on today, chats on the last read message, timelines on now — right on the first frame. Chromium only for now
mwg:scroll-target-on-load.support: scroll-initial-target: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 133, Edge 133. Unsupported in: Firefox, Safari

mwg:scroll-target-on-load:2.title: `scroll-initial-target` moves the view, not keyboard focus
mwg:scroll-target-on-load:2.action: If the target should also be the keyboard starting point, call `element.focus()` separately
mwg:scroll-target-on-load:2.blocker: The property only moves the visual scroll position; keyboard focus stays where it was (quote: "This property only moves the **visual** viewport; it does not move the keyboard focus.")
mwg:scroll-target-on-load:2.outcome: With focus moved manually, view and focus agree (official claim)
mwg:scroll-target-on-load:2.story: The view opened on today, but one Tab jumped back to the first link at the top.

mwg:scroll-target-on-load:3.title: Give media before the initial target its dimensions
mwg:scroll-target-on-load:3.action: Set `aspect-ratio` or fixed `width`/`height` on images and videos
mwg:scroll-target-on-load:3.blocker: The scroll position is computed during initial layout; media that loads later grows and pushes the target away (quote: "ensure images or videos have `aspect-ratio` or fixed `height`/`width` to prevent the target from shifting after the media loads.")
mwg:scroll-target-on-load:3.outcome: With space reserved, the target stays where it was computed (official claim)
mwg:scroll-target-on-load:3.story: The feed did open on the featured item, then the images above it loaded and pushed it off-screen.

mwg:scroll-target-on-load:4.title: URL fragments and `scroll-start` override `scroll-initial-target`; set only one per container
mwg:scroll-target-on-load:4.action: Give only one element per scroll container `scroll-initial-target`; remember that URL fragments and the container's `scroll-start` take precedence
mwg:scroll-target-on-load:4.blocker: With several elements set, only the first in DOM order is used; with a fragment in the URL the property is ignored (quote: "A URL fragment (e.g., `example.com/#top`) and the container-level `scroll-start` property both take precedence over `scroll-initial-target`.")
mwg:scroll-target-on-load:4.outcome: Knowing the precedence makes the starting position predictable (official claim)
mwg:scroll-target-on-load:4.story: A shared link carried `#top`, so the recipient's list opened at the top instead of the featured item.

mwg:scrollytelling.title: Use named `view-timeline`s and `timeline-scope` so one set of sections drives another set's animations
mwg:scrollytelling.action: Put named timelines like `view-timeline: --tl-1 block` on the tracked sections, publish them with `timeline-scope` on a common ancestor (often `html`), bind the animated elements with `animation-timeline: --tl-1`, and set exact ranges with `animation-range`
mwg:scrollytelling.blocker: The guide doesn't say what breaks in the old approach; it only says this needs no JavaScript and follows scroll position rather than a clock (quote: "The animations are controlled by the scroll position, not a time-based clock, which ensures they are always in sync with the user's scroll.")
mwg:scrollytelling.outcome: Pure CSS lets text sections drive the images on the other side; scroll-driven animations are Newly available, with IntersectionObserver plus many thresholds as fallback (official claim)
mwg:scrollytelling.story: Text on the left, a picture on the right that changes with each section. The text is the timeline and the picture the animation; they needn't be parent and child — timeline-scope ties them together.
mwg:scrollytelling.unlock: "Read this paragraph and the graphic changes" used to need a library like scrollama → year-in-review pages, product tours and data journalism can let each paragraph drive a pinned layer, rewinding when scrolled back

mwg:scrollytelling:2.title: Add `animation-range: 0% 100%` to the check to filter partial support
mwg:scrollytelling:2.blocker: Checking only `animation-timeline` lets partially supporting browsers through (quote: "The `(animation-range: 0% 100%)` check **MUST** be included here, to filter out browsers with only partial support.")
mwg:scrollytelling:2.outcome: Partially supporting browsers take the fallback (official claim)
mwg:scrollytelling:2.story: Detection said yes, but the ranges were ignored and the image appeared at the wrong section.

mwg:scrollytelling:3.title: Put `animation-timeline` after the `animation` shorthand
mwg:scrollytelling:3.action: Write the `animation` shorthand first, then `animation-timeline` and `animation-range`
mwg:scrollytelling:3.blocker: The shorthand resets the timeline (quote: "declare `animation-timeline` and `animation-range` *after* it to prevent the shorthand from resetting the timeline.")
mwg:scrollytelling:3.outcome: In the right order the timeline is kept (official claim)
mwg:scrollytelling:3.story: Every section's animation played through by itself on load.

mwg:scrollytelling:4.title: Content must stay visible if the fallback script doesn't run or reduced motion is requested
mwg:scrollytelling:4.action: Attach the fallback's "hidden first" styles only to a `.scroll-fallback` class added by script; under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` force `opacity: 1` and `transform: none`
mwg:scrollytelling:4.blocker: Hiding sections by default while waiting for animation leaves content invisible forever if the script doesn't run (quote: "The CSS only hides the sections once this class is set, so they stay visible if the script doesn't run")
mwg:scrollytelling:4.outcome: If the script fails or motion is reduced, the story remains fully readable (official claim)
mwg:scrollytelling:4.story: The script was blocked and the whole right column stayed blank; half the story was missing.

mwg:search-hidden-content.title: Hide content with `<details>` or `hidden="until-found"` so find-in-page still reaches it
mwg:search-hidden-content.action: Prefer `<details>` for ordinary disclosure; when the controls live elsewhere in the DOM, styling must be fully custom, or content won't be re-hidden, use `hidden="until-found"` and sync related state in `beforematch` (e.g. set `aria-expanded="true"`, close other panels)
mwg:search-hidden-content.blocker: Content hidden with `display: none` or `visibility: hidden` is completely unreachable to screen readers and Find in page (quote: "they also make that content completely inaccessible to screen readers and browser features like "Find in page".")
mwg:search-hidden-content.outcome: Hidden content can be found by find-in-page, URL fragments and Scroll to Text Fragment links and is revealed automatically; `<details>` is Widely available, `hidden="until-found"` is unsupported in Safari, where the fallback expands everything (official claim)
mwg:search-hidden-content.story: Text inside tabs and custom accordions couldn't be found with Ctrl+F, and shared text-fragment links didn't open. With until-found the browser reveals the match itself and fires beforematch so buttons can catch up.
mwg:search-hidden-content.unlock: Custom tab contents used to be invisible to search → settings pages with many tabs, tabbed code samples on docs sites and product spec switchers can be hit directly by Ctrl+F and text-fragment links that switch to the right tab. Safari falls back to expanding everything
mwg:search-hidden-content.support: <details>: Widely. hidden="until-found": Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 102, Edge 102, Firefox 148. Unsupported in: Safari

mwg:search-hidden-content:2.title: Don't add `display` or `visibility` to `hidden="until-found"` elements
mwg:search-hidden-content:2.action: Leave hiding entirely to `hidden="until-found"`; don't add `display: none`, `visibility: hidden` or similar
mwg:search-hidden-content:2.blocker: Those styles break the native behaviour and remove the content from the search index for good (quote: "This breaks the native functionality and permanently hides the content from the search index.")
mwg:search-hidden-content:2.outcome: Without overrides, search finds and reveals it (official claim)
mwg:search-hidden-content:2.story: An extra `display: none` "to be safe" made until-found do nothing.

mwg:search-hidden-content:3.title: Put borders, padding and backgrounds on an inner wrapper, not the until-found element
mwg:search-hidden-content:3.action: Apply borders, padding and backgrounds to a child wrapper
mwg:search-hidden-content:3.blocker: Applied directly to the `hidden="until-found"` element they leave layout shifts or visual remnants while hidden (quote: "This prevents unintended layout shifts or visual remnants while the element is hidden.")
mwg:search-hidden-content:3.outcome: Hidden panels leave no trace (official claim)
mwg:search-hidden-content:3.story: A collapsed panel still showed an empty border and a strip of height.

mwg:search-hidden-content:4.title: Don't hide sensitive or irrelevant data with `hidden="until-found"`
mwg:search-hidden-content:4.action: Keep sensitive information, internal data tokens and content that shouldn't be searchable out of until-found sections
mwg:search-hidden-content:4.blocker: until-found content is found and revealed by find-in-page (quote: "**DO NOT** use `hidden="until-found"` for sensitive information, internal data tokens, or irrelevant data that should not be exposed via search.")
mwg:search-hidden-content:4.outcome: Kept out, it can't be revealed by search (official claim)
mwg:search-hidden-content:4.story: Thinking hidden meant safe, internal fields were turned up by a user's search.

mwg:spatial-navigation.title: Don't `preventDefault()` when there is no candidate in that direction; let the browser scroll
mwg:spatial-navigation.action: Intercept arrow keys only in composite widgets; only when a candidate is found call `preventDefault()`, move the roving tabindex and `scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', inline: 'nearest' })`; otherwise return; ignore modifier keys, already-handled events and targets that use arrows themselves (editable fields, sliders)
mwg:spatial-navigation.blocker: Overriding arrow keys unconditionally kills native scrolling and breaks accessibility (quote: "Overriding arrow keys unconditionally breaks accessibility (WCAG 1.4.10).")
mwg:spatial-navigation.outcome: Arrow keys at the edge go back to the browser to scroll the viewport (official claim)
mwg:spatial-navigation.story: A media rail got arrow-key navigation; with focus on the last row, pressing Down no longer scrolled the page.
mwg:spatial-navigation.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:spatial-navigation:2.title: Pick the next focus from live geometry on each keypress, not index or DOM order
mwg:spatial-navigation:2.action: On keypress read `getBoundingClientRect()` for the current and candidate elements (no caching), test direction by edges, prefer candidates overlapping on the perpendicular axis, else score `gap + w * perpendicular offset`; only consider elements passing `checkVisibility()`
mwg:spatial-navigation:2.blocker: In asymmetric, wrapped or grid layouts index mapping picks wrong; hidden elements can have a zero-size rect at `(0, 0)` and become accidental up/left targets (quote: "In asymmetrical, wrapped, or grid layouts, index-based mapping fails."; "Hidden elements can have a zero-sized rect at `(0, 0)` and must not become accidental `up` or `left` targets.")
mwg:spatial-navigation:2.outcome: Focus moves along the visually adjacent row or column (official claim)
mwg:spatial-navigation:2.story: Wide and narrow cards mixed: Right jumped to the start of the next line, and a hidden button made Up fly to the top-left corner.
mwg:spatial-navigation:2.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:spatial-navigation:3.title: Roving tabindex needs composite-widget roles; screen readers ignore tabindex alone
mwg:spatial-navigation:3.action: Give the container and items roles that fit the use: `grid`/`gridcell`, `tablist`, `listbox`/`option`, `tree`, `treegrid` or `combobox`
mwg:spatial-navigation:3.blocker: Without matching roles, roving tabindex doesn't work with screen readers (quote: "Roving tabindex only works with screen readers when the container and items have appropriate composite-widget roles and states (e.g. grid/gridcell, listbox/option); tabindex alone isn't enough.")
mwg:spatial-navigation:3.outcome: With roles and states, screen readers understand the single tab stop and arrow movement (official claim)
mwg:spatial-navigation:3.story: Keyboard users loved it; screen reader users heard a pile of unrelated buttons and never learned arrows worked.
mwg:spatial-navigation:3.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:spatial-navigation:4.title: Use `composedPath()[0]` to find where the key came from, not just `e.target`
mwg:spatial-navigation:4.action: Take the innermost target with `e.composedPath()[0]` and check it against `:read-write, select, input[type="range"], [role="slider"]` to see if it uses arrows itself
mwg:spatial-navigation:4.blocker: `e.target` can be retargeted to a shadow host, hiding that the key came from an input inside (quote: "Use `e.composedPath()[0]` rather than only `e.target`, because `e.target` can be retargeted to a shadow host.")
mwg:spatial-navigation:4.outcome: Inputs inside web components keep their own arrow behaviour (closed shadow roots still can't be inspected) (official claim)
mwg:spatial-navigation:4.story: Pressing Left inside a custom element's text field to move the caret jumped focus to the neighbouring card.
mwg:spatial-navigation:4.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:swipe-to-remove.title: Build swipe-to-remove with scroll snap and IntersectionObserver, not hand-written pointer events
mwg:swipe-to-remove.action: Make each row a three-column (left spacer, content, right spacer) horizontal track with `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory`; an IntersectionObserver rooted at the track watches the content, popping the icon below `activateThreshold` and committing with the collapse animation below `commitThreshold`
mwg:swipe-to-remove.blocker: Driving a transform yourself with `pointerdown`/`pointermove`/`pointerup` loses the momentum, snap-back and keyboard scrolling native scrolling gives for free (quote: "You'll lose the momentum, snap-back, and keyboard scrolling that native scrolling gives you for free.")
mwg:swipe-to-remove.outcome: The gesture belongs to the browser's scroll engine, so momentum and snapping are native; scroll snap, IntersectionObserver, MutationObserver and Web Animations are all Widely available (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-remove.story: A hand-built swipe-to-delete didn't coast after release and judged speed oddly. Making the row a snapping horizontal scroller gives native feel; the code only watches how much content is still on screen.
mwg:swipe-to-remove.support: Scroll snap, Intersection observer, MutationObserver, Web animations: Baseline Widely available

mwg:swipe-to-remove:2.title: Set `overscroll-behavior-x: none` on the track to stop over-swipes triggering Back
mwg:swipe-to-remove:2.action: Set `overscroll-behavior-x: none` on each row's horizontal track
mwg:swipe-to-remove:2.blocker: Without it, an over-swipe can trigger the iOS/Android back-navigation gesture (quote: "Without it, an over-swipe can trigger the browser's back-navigation gesture on iOS/Android.")
mwg:swipe-to-remove:2.outcome: The swipe stays inside the row; the guide lists overscroll-behavior as Limited but says the track is always scrollable here, so behaviour is consistent and needs no fallback (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-remove:2.story: A hard swipe right to archive an email sent the whole page back to the previous one.
mwg:swipe-to-remove:2.support: overscroll-behavior: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 144, Edge 144, Firefox 150. Unsupported in: Safari (the guide notes this only affects containers without scrollable overflow)

mwg:swipe-to-remove:3.title: Use `mandatory` snapping, not `proximity`
mwg:swipe-to-remove:3.action: Set `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory` on the track
