mwg:swipe-to-remove:3.blocker: `proximity` lets the row rest half-scrolled with the action background half visible (quote: "With `proximity`, the row can rest partially scrolled, leaving the action background half-visible.")
mwg:swipe-to-remove:3.outcome: The row always rests on the content or a spacer (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-remove:3.story: A light flick left one row stuck half-open with a strip of red showing.

mwg:swipe-to-remove:4.title: Give every swipe action a visible button alternative
mwg:swipe-to-remove:4.action: Put a native button of at least 24×24 CSS px in each row, named with the item, that runs the same `commit` function as the swipe
mwg:swipe-to-remove:4.blocker: Swiping can't be done by keyboard, single tap or screen reader; swipe-only functions fail the pointer-gestures criterion (quote: "functionality must not be available solely through swiping gestures.")
mwg:swipe-to-remove:4.outcome: Voice control, keyboard and screen reader users can perform the same action (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-remove:4.story: A voice control user could say "delete" but not swipe, so the email could never be deleted.
mwg:swipe-to-remove:4.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:swipe-to-remove:5.title: Don't make the track focusable when the row has buttons, and offer undo
mwg:swipe-to-remove:5.action: Don't add `tabindex` to the track of rows that already have action buttons; consider an undo toast after removal
mwg:swipe-to-remove:5.blocker: A focused track commits the action on arrow keys with no confirmation, and the swipe is easy to trigger by accident (quote: "arrow keys on a focused track commit the action with no confirmation."; "the gesture is fast and easy to trigger by accident.")
mwg:swipe-to-remove:5.outcome: Keyboard deletion only happens through the button, and mistakes can be undone (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-remove:5.story: A keyboard user tabbed to a row, pressed an arrow to look further, and the row was deleted.
mwg:swipe-to-remove:5.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:swipe-to-remove:6.title: In Safari, removing a node mid-momentum makes the next row scroll itself away
mwg:swipe-to-remove:6.action: When `GestureEvent` (Safari-only) exists, mark the row `inert` and delay the actual `remove()` by a few seconds
mwg:swipe-to-remove:6.blocker: Safari's scroll-latching bug: removing the node while momentum is still resolving lets the next row inherit the scroll and immediately scroll off-screen (quote: "causes the next item (which slides up into this one's place) to inherit the scroll and immediately scroll itself off-screen.")
mwg:swipe-to-remove:6.outcome: Delaying removal avoids it, at the cost of the node staying in the DOM a few seconds longer (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-remove:6.story: Deleting one email on an iPhone also slid the next one away, looking like two deletions.
mwg:swipe-to-remove:6.support: Browser bug; no support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:swipe-to-remove:7.title: Apply `scroll-initial-target` only once the track is actually a scroll container
mwg:swipe-to-remove:7.action: Scope the content's `scroll-initial-target: nearest` under the `.is-initialized` selector so it only applies after JS has wired the row
mwg:swipe-to-remove:7.blocker: Before the track is a scroll container, the property walks up to the nearest scrollable ancestor (usually the page) and changes the page's initial scroll (quote: "would let the property walk up to the nearest scrollable ancestor (typically the document) and shift the page's initial scroll position")
mwg:swipe-to-remove:7.outcome: The property only acts on the row's own track (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-remove:7.story: The list sat mid-page, yet opening the page scrolled straight to one of its rows.
mwg:swipe-to-remove:7.support: scroll-initial-target: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 133, Edge 133. Unsupported in: Firefox, Safari

mwg:swipe-to-remove:8.title: Run the fallback's programmatic scroll before attaching the observer
mwg:swipe-to-remove:8.action: Without `scroll-initial-target`, set `track.scrollLeft = track.clientWidth` after adding `.is-initialized` and before attaching the inner IntersectionObserver; re-apply with a ResizeObserver on resize and unobserve before removal
mwg:swipe-to-remove:8.blocker: In the wrong order the initial programmatic scroll is seen as a swipe and commits immediately (quote: "Otherwise the initial programmatic scroll past the left spacer will be observed as a "swipe" and immediately fire the commit handler.")
mwg:swipe-to-remove:8.outcome: In the right order rows rest quietly on their content (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-remove:8.story: Opening the inbox in Firefox, every row deleted itself as soon as it appeared.

mwg:swipe-to-remove:9.title: Set up each row when it enters the viewport, and wire later rows with MutationObserver
mwg:swipe-to-remove:9.action: An outer IntersectionObserver calls `setupItem()` the first time a row enters view and pauses the inner observer when it leaves; a MutationObserver on the `<ul>` registers newly added rows
mwg:swipe-to-remove:9.blocker: Wiring everything at load reads `clientWidth` as 0 before rows render, and rows added later never get wired (quote: "`setupItem` reads layout-dependent values like `clientWidth`, which return 0 until the item is rendered"; "Without it, items appended after page load won't get wired up.")
mwg:swipe-to-remove:9.outcome: Every row gets real dimensions and the observer count stays proportional to what is visible (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-remove:9.story: New emails from infinite scroll wouldn't swipe, and older ones' fallback scroll went to 0.

mwg:swipe-to-remove:10.title: Write the removal result into a `role="status"` that was already on the page
mwg:swipe-to-remove:10.action: Render an empty `role="status"` from the start and write e.g. "Item One removed" into it on removal
mwg:swipe-to-remove:10.blocker: A row disappearing isn't announced, and screen readers only announce changes to live regions that existed before the change (quote: "A row disappearing isn't announced"; "screen readers only announce changes to live regions that existed before the change.")
mwg:swipe-to-remove:10.outcome: Screen reader users learn which item was removed (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-remove:10.story: A screen reader user pressed Remove, heard nothing, and couldn't tell whether it worked.
mwg:swipe-to-remove:10.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:swipe-to-remove:11.title: Before removing the focused row, move focus to the next row
mwg:swipe-to-remove:11.action: If focus is inside the row, move it to the next row (or previous, or the list heading) before removal, keeping the same kind of element (track to track, button to button)
mwg:swipe-to-remove:11.blocker: Removing or inerting the row containing focus drops focus to `<body>` (quote: "Removing or inerting the row drops focus to <body> if focus is inside it")
mwg:swipe-to-remove:11.outcome: Keyboard users can carry on with the next row (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-remove:11.story: After deleting an email with the button, the next Tab started from the top of the page.
mwg:swipe-to-remove:11.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:swipe-to-remove:12.title: In forced colors, paint the action icon with `CanvasText` through a mask
mwg:swipe-to-remove:12.action: Under `@media (forced-colors: active)` set `forced-color-adjust: none`, use `CanvasText` as the background and the icon as a `mask`
mwg:swipe-to-remove:12.blocker: Forced colors replaces the action background with `Canvas`, hiding the white icon (quote: "Forced colors replaces the action background with Canvas, which hides the white icon.")
mwg:swipe-to-remove:12.outcome: The icon stays visible in forced colors (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-remove:12.story: A high-contrast user swiped a row open and saw only blank space, with no hint of what would happen.
mwg:swipe-to-remove:12.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:swipe-to-reveal.title: Build swipe-to-reveal with scroll snap; don't intercept wheel, touchmove or pointermove
mwg:swipe-to-reveal.action: Make the outer `.SwipeReveal` a two-column grid (`100% max-content`) horizontal scroller with `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory`; content snaps to `start`, the action panel to `end`
mwg:swipe-to-reveal.blocker: Intercepting gestures on the main thread to translate content yourself blocks compositor scrolling, breaks momentum and hurts responsiveness (quote: "Main-thread gesture interception blocks compositor-driven scrolling, breaks native scroll momentum, and degrades responsiveness.")
mwg:swipe-to-reveal.outcome: Momentum, snapping, keyboard focus scrolling and scroll chaining are handled by the browser with no gesture listeners (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-reveal.story: A hand-built swipe list stuttered on low-end phones and stopped stiffly after release. As a snapping horizontal scroller, it opens with native-app feel.

mwg:swipe-to-reveal:2.title: Use `overscroll-behavior: chain` on the outer swipe wrapper: scroll still chains, but no bounce
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:2.action: Set `overscroll-behavior: chain` on the outer `.SwipeReveal`; keep the default `auto` on inner scrollable content panes
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:2.blocker: The default `auto` makes the outer wrapper rubber-band and the menu bounce with it; `contain` or `none` trap scrolling so it never reaches the page (quote: "avoid on the outer swipe wrapper where it causes the menu to bounce")
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:2.outcome: In supporting browsers excess scroll passes to the parent and the action strip no longer bounces; `chain` is Limited, and browsers that don't recognise it drop it at parse time and keep `auto`, still working but bouncing (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:2.story: Swiping the action strip open made it rubber-band, buttons and all, which felt cheap. You used to choose between "bounces" and "traps scroll"; the new keyword separates chaining from bouncing.
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:2.unlock: Nested scrollers used to force a choice between bouncing and trapping → vertical feeds can contain swipe-to-act rows, side-swipeable cards or horizontal chip rows that don't bounce at the edge and hand extra scroll to the page. Safari still bounces
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:2.support: overscroll-behavior: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 144, Edge 144, Firefox 150. Unsupported in: Safari

mwg:swipe-to-reveal:3.title: Snap the reveal panel with `mandatory`, not `proximity`
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:3.action: Set `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory` on the outer wrapper
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:3.blocker: With `proximity`, a light swipe can leave the buttons or side menu half exposed (quote: "With `proximity`, a light swipe can leave the action buttons or side menu partially exposed at rest.")
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:3.outcome: The panel is either fully open or fully closed (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:3.story: Several rows showed half a "Delete" button.

mwg:swipe-to-reveal:4.title: Actions revealed by swiping need a trigger button that opens them
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:4.action: Put a trigger button named with the item (`aria-expanded`) in the content; on press scroll to the panel and set the panel buttons' `tabindex` to 0; reverse on second press
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:4.blocker: Functions only reachable by swiping fail the pointer-gestures criterion (quote: "functionality must not be available solely through swiping gestures.")
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:4.outcome: Keyboard and voice control users can open and use the panel via the button (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:4.story: A keyboard user knew every row had "Pin" and "Archive" but found no way to open them.
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:4.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:swipe-to-reveal:5.title: Use `scroll-initial-target` so rows with a leading panel start on the content column
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:5.action: With panels on both sides (`max-content 100% max-content`), place the leading panel before the content and set `scroll-initial-target: nearest` on the content
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:5.blocker: Unsupported browsers render at scroll offset 0 with the leading panel exposed (quote: "browsers that do not support `scroll-initial-target: nearest` will initially render at scroll offset `0` with the leading panel exposed.")
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:5.outcome: Supporting browsers start on the content column; Chrome/Edge 133 only, others need `scrollTo({ behavior: 'instant' })` on `load` (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:5.story: Mail rows with swipe-left-to-archive and swipe-right-to-delete opened in Safari with every archive button already showing.
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:5.unlock: Two-sided swipe rows used to need JS to scroll to the middle first → mail, to-do and chat lists can have one set of actions on the left and another on the right in pure CSS, resting in the middle on load. Chromium only for now
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:5.support: scroll-initial-target: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 133, Edge 133. Unsupported in: Firefox, Safari

mwg:swipe-to-reveal:6.title: When overriding an existing `contain`/`none`, declare `auto` right before `chain`
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:6.action: If base styles set `overscroll-behavior: contain` or `none`, declare `overscroll-behavior: auto` immediately before `overscroll-behavior: chain`
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:6.blocker: Browsers that don't recognise `chain` drop the line and keep the earlier `contain`/`none`, trapping scroll (quote: "declare `overscroll-behavior: auto` immediately before `overscroll-behavior: chain` so browsers that do not yet support `chain` still chain scrolling to the parent rather than trapping it.")
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:6.outcome: Unsupported browsers fall back to `auto` and still chain to the parent (official claim)
mwg:swipe-to-reveal:6.story: A utility class defaulted to `overscroll-behavior: none`; in Safari, swiping up or down on that row moved nothing.

mwg:card.title: When a card has a lot of text or other actions, use a stretched link instead of wrapping it in `<a>`
mwg:card.action: Wrap the `<article>` in one `<a>` only when the whole card is one destination and the text is short; otherwise make only the heading's `.card-link` a link and stretch its hit area with `::after` and `inset: 0`
mwg:card.blocker: When the whole card is inside the link, the link's accessible name is all of the card's text (quote: "Because the link's accessible name is all of the card's text, keep the content short")
mwg:card.outcome: The link name is just the heading while the whole card stays clickable (official claim)
mwg:card.story: Screen reader users had to hear the whole summary, author and date in the link list to learn which article it was. Making only the heading a link and stretching the hit area fixes both hearing and clicking.
mwg:card.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:card:2.title: "Read more" links need a full name that starts with the visible text
mwg:card:2.action: Write `Read more(visually hidden) about poached eggs`; add no other links repeating the heading's URL
mwg:card:2.blocker: Identical "read more" links can't be told apart in a screen reader's link list (quote: "identical "read more" links are ambiguous in a screen reader's link list.")
mwg:card:2.outcome: Each link name identifies its destination (official claim)
mwg:card:2.story: The link list showed ten "Read more" entries.
mwg:card:2.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:card:3.title: Don't change layout-affecting properties when a choice card is selected
mwg:card:3.action: Put a checkbox or radio in `<label class="card">` and use `:has(> :checked)` to change only a transparent border's colour, `outline` or `box-shadow`
mwg:card:3.blocker: Changing `border-width`, `padding` or `font-weight` on selection makes the card and its neighbours jump (quote: "Never change layout-affecting properties such as `border-width`, `padding`, or `font-weight` on selection, because the card and its neighbors jump")
mwg:card:3.outcome: Selection only changes colour; the layout stays still (official claim)
mwg:card:3.story: Selecting a plan card nudged the whole row two pixels to the right.
mwg:card:3.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:card:4.title: Only one stretched link per card; lift other interactive elements individually
mwg:card:4.action: Add `.card-link` to exactly one link per card; give other `a`, `button`, `input` etc. `position: relative; z-index: 1` by element type, never `z-index` on whole containers
mwg:card:4.blocker: With several stretched links the last one covers the card; `z-index` on a whole container captures clicks that do nothing (quote: "each would stretch its own overlay and the last one would capture the whole card"; "Do NOT apply `z-index` to entire containers as that would make them capture pointer events that don't produce any action.")
mwg:card:4.outcome: Clicks elsewhere on the card go to the main link, and buttons work on their own (official claim)
mwg:card:4.story: Clicking "Save" on a card opened the article; clicking the footer's empty space did nothing.
mwg:card:4.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:card:5.title: Lay out cards with the card itself as the query container, not the viewport or grid parent
mwg:card:5.action: Set `container-type: inline-size` on the card and adapt children with `@container` rules; open a media side column only on cards with media via `:has(> img)`
mwg:card:5.blocker: A card's real width depends on column count, gaps and so on, so parent-based breakpoints are unreliable (quote: "the card's actual width can depend on column count, gaps and so on, making parent-based breakpoints are noisy.")
mwg:card:5.outcome: Narrow cards stack in source order and wide ones put media at the side, wherever they are placed (official claim)
mwg:card:5.story: The same card was cramped in a three-column grid but used the wide layout in a sidebar.
mwg:card:5.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:checkbox.title: Restyle checkboxes with `accent-color` or `appearance: none` while keeping the native `<input>`
mwg:checkbox.action: Use `accent-color` for a simple brand colour (keeping native rendering, keyboard, validation and system focus rings); for control over shape, size and states set `appearance: none` on `<input type="checkbox">` and draw the check and `:indeterminate` dash with `::before` and `mask`
mwg:checkbox.blocker: The guide doesn't say what breaks in the old approach; it only says both techniques keep native behaviour or keep the `<input>` as the interactive target (quote: "This removes the native visual styling while leaving the `<input>` as the interactive target.")
mwg:checkbox.outcome: Both keep native interaction; the guide labels `accent-color` Limited and calls it progressive enhancement, falling back to default colours (official claim)
mwg:checkbox.story: Branded checkboxes were often a div plus an icon. Now one accent-color line recolours them, and bolder designs can be drawn on the input itself with keyboard, forms and screen readers untouched.
mwg:checkbox.unlock: Branded checkboxes used to mean a custom component → to-do lists, permission settings and bulk "select all (partial)" states can use native inputs that match the design, with a proper indeterminate icon
mwg:checkbox.support: accent-color: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 93, Edge 93, Firefox 92, Safari 26.2 (labelled Limited though all four engines are listed, as in mwg:brand-consistent-forms); Masks: Widely

mwg:checkbox:2.title: Safari's `accent-color` doesn't guarantee check-mark contrast; test it
mwg:checkbox:2.action: Test important accent colours in Safari in both light and dark schemes, keeping checked and indeterminate states at 3:1 contrast or more
mwg:checkbox:2.blocker: Safari may keep a white (light) or black (dark) check and adjust the accent behind it, which doesn't always give enough contrast (quote: "This adjustment does not always provide sufficient contrast for every supplied color")
mwg:checkbox:2.outcome: Tested combinations can be confirmed; the guide offers no automatic fix (official claim)
mwg:checkbox:2.story: Brand yellow with a black check was clear in Chrome; in Safari the check turned white and you could barely tell it was ticked.

mwg:checkbox:3.title: After `appearance: none`, give the checkbox a size yourself
mwg:checkbox:3.action: Set `--checkbox-size` and `--checkbox-icon-size` in relative units, with the icon smaller than the box
mwg:checkbox:3.blocker: `appearance: none` also removes the browser's default dimensions (quote: "`appearance: none` removes the browser’s default dimensions.")
mwg:checkbox:3.outcome: Box and check keep a fixed ratio and scale with text (official claim)
mwg:checkbox:3.story: Once the native look was removed, the checkbox shrank to an invisible dot.
mwg:checkbox:3.support: appearance: no support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:dark-mode-toggle.title: Changing `<meta name="color-scheme">` alone does nothing; map it back to CSS with `:has()`
mwg:dark-mode-toggle.action: Keep `color-scheme: light dark` on `:root`, then override it via `:root:has(> head > meta[name="color-scheme"][content="dark"])` (and `light`); the toggle only changes the meta's content
mwg:dark-mode-toggle.blocker: The `<meta>` is only a presentational hint and author CSS `color-scheme` overrides it, so updating the meta alone is a no-op (quote: "updating the `<meta>` alone is a **no-op** — CSS wins.")
mwg:dark-mode-toggle.outcome: `light-dark()`, system colours and native UI follow the override; without JS the meta stays `light dark` and follows the system (official claim)
mwg:dark-mode-toggle.story: The toggle changed the meta, and the page's colours didn't move. Wiring the meta back to the color-scheme property brings every colour along at once.
mwg:dark-mode-toggle.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:dark-mode-toggle:2.title: Apply the stored scheme with a synchronous inline script right after the `<meta>`
mwg:dark-mode-toggle:2.action: Place a tiny inline `<script>` (not a module, no defer) right after `<meta name="color-scheme">` that reads `localStorage` and writes it back to the meta
mwg:dark-mode-toggle:2.blocker: Applying the stored preference later flashes the wrong scheme first (quote: "To avoid a flash of the wrong scheme, apply the stored value in an inline script (NOT `type=module`, NOT `defer`) placed immediately after the `<meta>` element")
mwg:dark-mode-toggle:2.outcome: The first paint uses the user's chosen scheme (official claim)
mwg:dark-mode-toggle:2.story: A user who chose dark got flashed with white on every page load.
mwg:dark-mode-toggle:2.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:dark-mode-toggle:3.title: Compare with the system preference only when storing; never delete the stored value later just because they match
mwg:dark-mode-toggle:3.action: A two-state toggle targets the opposite of what is shown; store it only if it differs from the system preference, remove the stored value if it matches; keep stored values that later match the system and don't clear them with `matchMedia()`
mwg:dark-mode-toggle:3.blocker: Many systems switch by time of day, so deleting the stored value whenever they coincide makes pinning impossible; storing a value equal to the system silently pins it against future changes (quote: "removing the stored value whenever the two happen to coincide would make it impossible to pin a scheme at all."; "that would invisibly pin the scheme against future system changes.")
mwg:dark-mode-toggle:3.outcome: Users can pin a scheme and also return to following the system in one click (official claim)
mwg:dark-mode-toggle:3.story: Pinned to dark during the day, the preference was wiped when the OS turned dark at dusk, and the next morning the site was light again.
mwg:dark-mode-toggle:3.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:dark-mode-toggle:4.title: Don't branch non-colour values only on a JS-applied `.dark` class
mwg:dark-mode-toggle:4.action: Branch font weights, image sources and other non-colour values with the `prefers-color-scheme` media query combined with a `:root:has(> head > meta[...][content="dark"])` selector
mwg:dark-mode-toggle:4.blocker: If JS doesn't load and the OS default is dark, branches that rely only on `.dark` are wrong (quote: "they will be incorrect if JS doesn't load and the OS default is dark.")
mwg:dark-mode-toggle:4.outcome: Branches match the actual scheme whether or not JS runs (official claim)
mwg:dark-mode-toggle:4.story: Dark OS, script blocked: a dark background with the black logo meant for light backgrounds.
mwg:dark-mode-toggle:4.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:dialog.title: Use native `<dialog>` with `showModal()`; don't hand-write focus traps, inert or Esc
mwg:dialog.action: Open blocking confirmations, forms and sign-in as `<dialog>` via `command="show-modal"` or `showModal()`; add no `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, focus trap, `inert` toggling or Esc handler
mwg:dialog.blocker: The guide only says custom overlays must rebuild these behaviours by hand, not when the rebuilt version fails (quote: "It provides the accessibility semantics, focus handling, top-layer rendering and `Esc` handling that custom overlays have to rebuild by hand.")
mwg:dialog.outcome: The browser provides an inert page, focus containment, top layer, `::backdrop`, Esc and back-gesture dismissal, and focus return to the invoker (official claim)
mwg:dialog.story: Every project had its own modal component, each missing something different. Native dialog hands the whole bundle to the browser.
mwg:dialog.support: <dialog> itself: no support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:dialog:2.title: Stop background scrolling under a modal with `overscroll-behavior`, not by locking `<body>`
mwg:dialog:2.action: Set `overscroll-behavior: contain` on `dialog:modal`; set `overflow: hidden` plus `overscroll-behavior: contain` on `dialog::backdrop` (details in mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dialog)
mwg:dialog:2.blocker: Without both rules, scrolling over the backdrop or in the dialog scrolls the page behind; locking the root with `overflow: hidden` or `position: fixed` removes the scrollbar and shifts layout (quote: "without them, scrolling over the backdrop or inside the dialog scrolls the page behind it")
mwg:dialog:2.outcome: Supporting browsers fully block background scrolling; Safari only when the dialog content overflows, and this can't be feature-detected (official claim)
mwg:dialog:2.story: With a delete confirmation open, one swipe scrolled the list behind it away.
mwg:dialog:2.unlock: Same as mwg:prevent-page-scroll-under-modal-dialog: every modal (lightbox, confirmation, form) can lock background scroll in pure CSS without layout jumps
mwg:dialog:2.support: overscroll-behavior: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 144, Edge 144, Firefox 150. Unsupported in: Safari

mwg:dialog:3.title: Use `<dialog popover>` for panels people work alongside, not `showModal()`
mwg:dialog:3.action: For find bars, inspectors, palettes and compose panes, use `<dialog popover>` (`auto` light-dismisses, `manual` doesn't) with a visible close button; for menus, tooltips and hovercards use a semantic element with `popover`, not `<dialog>`
mwg:dialog:3.blocker: Opening such panels with `showModal()` blocks the whole page (quote: "**DON'T** use `showModal()`, which blocks the page.")
mwg:dialog:3.outcome: The panel sits in the top layer while the page stays interactive and not inert; Popover is Newly available (official claim)
mwg:dialog:3.story: Opening "Find" to search while clicking results locked the entire page until the dialog was closed.

mwg:dialog:4.title: Reset `returnValue` to an empty string after reading it
mwg:dialog:4.action: In the `close` listener read `dialog.returnValue` to see which button was used, then set `dialog.returnValue = ''`, treating empty as "dismissed without choosing"
mwg:dialog:4.blocker: Esc and other close requests set no value and browsers differ on clearing the previous one, so a stale value leaks into this close (quote: "browsers differ on whether they clear the previous one, so without the reset a stale value can leak.")
mwg:dialog:4.outcome: Each close only sees this time's choice (official claim)
mwg:dialog:4.story: Last time "Delete" was pressed; this time Esc closed the dialog, and the code deleted another item.
mwg:dialog:4.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:dialog:5.title: When closing is blocked, tell the user why the dialog stayed open
mwg:dialog:5.action: When `cancel` is prevented, show a visible message and reference it with `aria-describedby` from the control that receives focus (such as Discard)
mwg:dialog:5.blocker: Without it, focus moving to a new button announces only that button's name (quote: "Without it, focus moving to a new button announces only that button's name.")
mwg:dialog:5.outcome: Screen readers read the reason when focus moves (official claim)
mwg:dialog:5.story: Esc didn't close the dialog and the screen reader only said "Discard, button"; the user had no idea what happened.
mwg:dialog:5.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:dialog:6.title: Don't move buttons under the pointer when the confirmation appears
mwg:dialog:6.action: Reserve the message's space (hide it with `visibility`, not `display` or `hidden`) and add the destructive button where existing buttons don't move
mwg:dialog:6.blocker: If the layout shifts, a second click at the same spot hits Discard and throws away the user's changes (quote: "so a second click at the same spot cannot discard the user's changes.")
mwg:dialog:6.outcome: Buttons stay put, so repeated clicks can't hit the destructive action (official claim)
mwg:dialog:6.story: A double-click on "Cancel" landed its second click on the newly appeared "Discard changes".
mwg:dialog:6.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:dialog:7.title: Don't set `display` on `dialog` unconditionally
mwg:dialog:7.blocker: Setting it on `dialog` overrides the closed state (quote: "It overrides the closed state. Scope it with `dialog[open]`.")
mwg:dialog:7.story: `dialog { display: flex }` for layout left the dialog open from page load onwards.
mwg:dialog:7.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:dialog:8.title: Guard unsaved changes in `cancel`, not with `closedby="none"` alone
mwg:dialog:8.action: With unsaved changes set `closedby="none"` and also prevent and confirm in a `cancel` listener; use `command="request-close"` or `requestClose()` for Cancel buttons
mwg:dialog:8.blocker: Browsers without `closedby` ignore `closedby="none"`, so Esc still fires `cancel` and closes the dialog (quote: "`closedby="none"` is ignored the same way: `Esc` fires `cancel` and then closes the dialog.")
mwg:dialog:8.outcome: The `cancel` guard works in every browser; `closedby` is Limited (official claim)
mwg:dialog:8.story: Halfway through a long form in Safari, a stray Esc wiped everything.
mwg:dialog:8.support: <dialog closedby>: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 134, Edge 134, Firefox 141. Unsupported in: Safari

mwg:hovercard.title: Use `interestfor` so a link shows its preview card on both hover and focus
mwg:hovercard.action: Add `interestfor="card id"` to the trigger link and `popover="hint"` to the card; tune open/close delays with `interest-delay`, and set the start delay to 0 via `:root:has(:interest-source)` when a card is already open
mwg:hovercard.blocker: The guide doesn't say what breaks in the old approach; it only says this ensures the card appears on hover and focus (quote: "This ensures the card appears on both hover and focus.")
mwg:hovercard.outcome: Shown on hover and focus with a default half-second delay against accidental opening; Interest invokers are Chrome/Edge 149 only, elsewhere the guide loads the `interestfor` polyfill (official claim)
mwg:hovercard.story: Link preview cards mostly listened for mouseover, so keyboard users never saw them. One attribute makes hover and Tab open the same card, with delays handled in CSS.
mwg:hovercard.unlock: Preview cards used to need hand-written hover, focus, delay and close timers → wiki-style term previews, user profile cards and citation previews can be declarative and keyboard-reachable. Native only in Chromium, polyfill elsewhere
mwg:hovercard.support: Interest invokers: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 149, Edge 149. Unsupported in: Firefox, Safari

mwg:hovercard:2.title: Use `popover="hint"` for preview cards so open menus stay open
mwg:hovercard:2.blocker: With a regular popover, showing a preview card closes other open popover menus (quote: "Use `hint` to avoid closing unrelated popover menus that may be open.")
mwg:hovercard:2.outcome: Hints don't affect other popovers; `popover="hint"` is unsupported in Safari and falls back to `manual`, so a keyboard-opened card may stay open when another is opened by hover (official claim)
mwg:hovercard:2.story: With a menu open, moving the mouse over a link brought up the preview and the menu collapsed.
mwg:hovercard:2.unlock: Hints and menus used to close each other → toolbar menus can stay open while showing item explanations, and table filter panels can preview column definitions. Safari not yet supported
mwg:hovercard:2.support: popover="hint": Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 151, Edge 151, Firefox 153. Unsupported in: Safari

mwg:hovercard:3.title: When the hint repeats the trigger's name, add no ARIA
mwg:hovercard:3.action: Compare the normalised hint text with the trigger's accessible name and add no description if they match
mwg:hovercard:3.blocker: A description identical to the name is read twice (quote: "A description identical to the name would be read twice.")
mwg:hovercard:3.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:hovercard:4.title: Don't put `aria-expanded` on triggers that navigate or act
mwg:hovercard:4.action: For links and buttons with their own action, give the hint `role="tooltip"` and the trigger `aria-describedby`; use `aria-expanded` only on buttons whose job is opening the hint
mwg:hovercard:4.blocker: A trigger announced as "collapsed" implies Enter expands it, but Enter navigates or acts (quote: "A trigger announced as "collapsed" suggests `Enter` would expand it, but `Enter` navigates or acts.")
mwg:hovercard:4.outcome: Screen reader users correctly expect what Enter does (official claim)
mwg:hovercard:4.story: A screen reader user pressed Enter expecting the preview to expand and was taken to another page.
mwg:hovercard:4.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:hovercard:5.title: Hints exposed as descriptions may only carry content users can afford to miss
mwg:hovercard:5.action: Keep hovercards to supplementary information available elsewhere; anything users need goes in a toggletip or inline
mwg:hovercard:5.blocker: Not every screen reader reads descriptions while browsing; NVDA skips them in browse mode by design (quote: "Not every screen reader reads descriptions when moving through the page (NVDA skips them in browse mode by design)")
mwg:hovercard:5.outcome: Even if the description isn't read, nothing essential is lost (official claim)
mwg:hovercard:5.story: An important restriction lived only in the hovercard; NVDA users never heard it.
mwg:hovercard:5.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:hovercard:6.title: Wire ARIA once the DOM is parsed, not on focus, interest or after the polyfill
mwg:hovercard:6.action: Run a small script in every browser, before loading the `interestfor` polyfill and once the DOM is parsed, that adds ARIA to all `[interestfor]` triggers, and expose it for content inserted later
mwg:hovercard:6.blocker: Browse-mode screen readers need the attributes before any interaction, so wiring on focus or interest is too late, as is waiting for the polyfill, which wires only on `load` and adds no `role="tooltip"` to plain hints (quote: "wiring them lazily on `focus` or `interest` is too late, and so is waiting for the polyfill")
mwg:hovercard:6.outcome: Relationships are readable in browse mode from the start (official claim)
mwg:hovercard:6.story: A screen reader user arrowed through the whole page and no link had a description, because the attributes were only added on mouseover.

mwg:hovercard:7.title: Sync `aria-expanded` by listening for `toggle` in the capture phase on document
mwg:hovercard:7.action: Add one `capture: true` `toggle` listener on `document` that updates every script-owned trigger for that popover; don't sync from `interest`/`loseinterest`
mwg:hovercard:7.blocker: `toggle` doesn't bubble, so an ordinary listener on document never fires; and the popover can be closed by Esc, light dismiss or another trigger (quote: "`toggle` does not bubble. A bubbling listener on `document` never fires")
mwg:hovercard:7.outcome: State stays correct however the popover is closed (official claim)
mwg:hovercard:7.story: The hint was closed, but the screen reader still said "expanded".

mwg:hovercard:8.title: Use anchor positioning to keep the preview card under its link, flipping on overflow
mwg:hovercard:8.action: `interestfor` makes the trigger an implicit anchor; set `position-area: block-end span-inline-end` and `position-try-fallbacks: flip-block, flip-inline` on the card
mwg:hovercard:8.blocker: Without anchor positioning, popovers fall back to the default viewport-centred placement, detached from the trigger (quote: "tethered elements such as `[popover]` overlays fall back to their default user-agent placement (centered in the viewport for popovers).")
mwg:hovercard:8.outcome: The card sticks to the link and flips at viewport edges; core properties are Newly available, and without support you can load the polyfill (with explicit `anchor-name`) or fall back with `@supports` to centred or bottom-bar placement (official claim)
mwg:hovercard:8.story: The preview card appeared in the middle of the screen with no clue which link it belonged to. Anchor positioning grows it under the link and flips it near edges.
mwg:hovercard:8.unlock: Preview cards used to need Floating UI → link previews, people cards and footnote popups stick to their trigger and avoid edges with two lines of CSS
mwg:hovercard:8.support: Anchor positioning: recorded as Newly (core properties Baseline since 2026-01-13). The guide's "Supported by: Safari 27 … Unsupported in: Chrome, Edge, and Firefox" is a misleading group status (see lines/ui-components/app-menus.md); this line does not use `position-visibility`

mwg:hovercard:9.title: Without the polyfill, put `inset: auto` and `margin: 0` inside `@supports`
mwg:hovercard:9.action: Place `inset: auto`, `margin: 0` and `position-area` together inside `@supports (position-area: block-end)`, with an optional `@supports not (...)` fixed bottom bar
mwg:hovercard:9.blocker: Unsupported browsers ignore `position-area` but still apply `inset: auto`, overriding the default centring and stranding the popover at `(0, 0)` or over its trigger (quote: "leaving the popover stranded at `(0, 0)` or overlapping its trigger.")
mwg:hovercard:9.outcome: Without support, the default centring or a bottom bar is kept (official claim)
mwg:hovercard:9.story: In older browsers every preview card piled up in the top-left corner.
mwg:hovercard:9.support: Anchor positioning: recorded as Newly (misleading group status, see lines/ui-components/app-menus.md)

mwg:hovercard:10.title: Declare `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` separately after `transition`
mwg:hovercard:10.action: List `opacity, transform, display, overlay` in `transition`, then `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` on its own line; put entry values in `@starting-style`, all inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`
mwg:hovercard:10.blocker: Putting `allow-discrete` in the shorthand makes older browsers ignore the whole transition (quote: "Declare `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` as a separate property after `transition` rather than inside the `transition` shorthand so older browsers do not ignore the entire `transition` declaration.")
mwg:hovercard:10.outcome: Older browsers at least keep the plain fade (official claim)
mwg:hovercard:10.story: New browsers slid the card out elegantly; older ones lost even the basic fade.
mwg:hovercard:10.support: transition-behavior: no support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:hovercard:11.title: After clicking a preview card, morph it into the destination page with a cross-document transition
mwg:hovercard:11.action: Opt both pages into `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }`; give the card, title and image `view-transition-name` only inside `[popover]:popover-open`, with matching names on the destination; block rendering on the destination with `<link rel="expect" href="#main-content" blocking="render">` until key content is parsed
mwg:hovercard:11.blocker: If the destination renders before its content is parsed, the transition is unstable and flickers (quote: "To ensure the transition is stable and doesn't flicker, the destination page should use `blocking="render"` and `<link rel="expect">`")
mwg:hovercard:11.outcome: In supporting browsers the card's title and image fly straight into place on the destination; cross-document view transitions are unsupported in Firefox, which does a normal navigation (official claim)
mwg:hovercard:11.story: The preview already showed the title and hero image, yet clicking flashed the page white and redrew it. Names live only on the open card, so they never collide, and the destination waits for its main content before the snapshot.
mwg:hovercard:11.unlock: "Preview" and "open" used to be two disconnected screens → multi-page sites can let article previews and product quick-view cards grow into the full page on click, without becoming a SPA. Firefox does a normal navigation
mwg:hovercard:11.support: Cross-document view transitions: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 126, Edge 126, Safari 18.2. Unsupported in: Firefox

mwg:menu.title: Declare popup menus with `focusgroup="menu"` and `command="toggle-popover"`
mwg:menu.action: Give the trigger `commandfor` and `command="toggle-popover"`; the menu is the next-sibling `popover="auto"` containing `<div focusgroup="menu nomemory">`; don't write `role="menu"`/`menuitem` so focusgroup can infer them; submenus are another `popover="auto"` inside the parent focusgroup
mwg:menu.blocker: The guide only says not to add a second roving tabindex inside a focusgroup and that explicit roles block inference, not when a hand-written version fails (quote: "Do not add a second roving-tabindex system inside a focusgroup.")
mwg:menu.outcome: In supporting browsers focusgroup handles arrow movement and roles and invokers handle open, close and light dismiss; focusgroup is Chrome/Edge 150 only, elsewhere you install Up/Down/Home/End and roles yourself (official claim)
mwg:menu.story: Opening, closing, light dismiss, arrow keys and roles used to be your own JS. Now most of it is attributes; submenu preview and focus restoration are still script, and focusgroup is Chromium only.
mwg:menu.unlock: A "⋯" menu with a submenu used to need hundreds of lines of keyboard handling → table row action menus and an editor's Export submenu can be mostly declarative, with light dismiss and submenu relationships managed by the browser. focusgroup is Chromium only for now
mwg:menu.support: focusgroup: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 150, Edge 150. Unsupported in: Firefox, Safari. Invoker commands: Newly. Popover: Newly

mwg:menu:2.title: Anchor submenus beside their parent item; never fall back to viewport centring
mwg:menu:2.action: Top-level menus use `position-area: block-end span-inline-end`, submenus `position-area: inline-end span-block-end`, each with `position-try-fallbacks` flips; the implicit anchor comes from the invoker, so no `anchor-name`; without support, position from script under `@supports not`
mwg:menu:2.blocker: Without anchor positioning popovers fall back to viewport centring, detaching the menu from its trigger and letting a centred submenu cover its parent (quote: "it detaches the menu from its trigger, and a centered submenu covers its parent.")
mwg:menu:2.outcome: Menus stick to triggers and submenus sit beside parents, flipping on overflow; core properties are Newly available, older browsers need script positioning (official claim)
mwg:menu:2.story: Opening "Export ›" made the submenu jump to the centre of the screen, completely covering the menu you came from.
mwg:menu:2.unlock: Multi-level menus used to need a positioning library per level → file-manager context menus and an editor's nested Insert menu can cascade in pure CSS and flip at edges
mwg:menu:2.support: Anchor positioning: recorded as Newly (core properties Baseline since 2026-01-13). The guide's "Supported by: Safari 27 … Unsupported in: Chrome, Edge, and Firefox" is a misleading group status (see lines/ui-components/app-menus.md); this line does not use `position-visibility`

mwg:menu:3.title: Let the narrow-screen `--below` fallback shrink the submenu
mwg:menu:3.blocker: A fallback that doesn't fit is skipped; if none fit the base placement is kept, so a submenu a few pixels too wide silently covers its trigger (quote: "a submenu that is a few pixels too wide silently covers its trigger.")
mwg:menu:3.outcome: At 375px no submenu covers its own trigger (official claim)
mwg:menu:3.story: On a phone the Export submenu landed right on top of "Export", so there was nothing to tap to close it.
mwg:menu:3.support: Anchor positioning: recorded as Newly (misleading group status, see lines/ui-components/app-menus.md)

mwg:menu:4.title: Use `showPopover({ source })` plus a zero-size placeholder anchor for context menus and caret menus
mwg:menu:4.action: Open trigger-less menus with `showPopover({ source })`, passing the right-clicked card or the focused element; to open at a point (pointer, `@`-mention caret), keep an empty zero-size `position: fixed` element right before the menu, move it to the point on each open and pass it as `source`; name the menu with `aria-label`
mwg:menu:4.blocker: The guide only says to use anchor positioning rather than JavaScript coordinates, not when coordinates fail (quote: "Use CSS anchor positioning, not JavaScript coordinates.")
mwg:menu:4.outcome: The menu's corner lands on the point and flips near edges like a native context menu; the implicit anchor from `showPopover({ source })` is Newly available (official claim)
mwg:menu:4.story: Context menus and @-mention lists used to read pointer coordinates and compute viewport bounds. Moving an invisible dot to act as anchor lets the same CSS handle flipping.
mwg:menu:4.unlock: Context and caret menus used to need hand-computed coordinates and collision → kanban card context menus and chat-input @-mention and /command lists can share one CSS positioning setup that avoids edges
mwg:menu:4.support: showPopover() source parameter (implicit anchor): Baseline Newly available (since 2026-01-13)

mwg:menu:5.title: Draw the submenu "safe triangle" in CSS from where the pointer left to the submenu's edge
mwg:menu:5.action: Only under `(hover: hover)`, on `pointerleave` of a submenu trigger write the pointer position to `--pointer-x`/`--pointer-y` and set `data-bridge`; the submenu's `::before` uses `clip-path: polygon()` to draw a triangle from that point to the submenu's near corners (side picked with `sign()`), removed after about 300 ms at rest, on turning away, or on reaching an item
mwg:menu:5.blocker: A static CSS bridge is too narrow and only works if the pointer starts near the parent's edge; a diagonal move crosses sibling items and closes the submenu (quote: "A static CSS bridge is too narrow: it only works when the pointer starts near the parent's edge.")
mwg:menu:5.outcome: Diagonal moves to a submenu item keep it open, while moving to an unrelated sibling closes it; `sign()` is Newly available with a `clamp()` fallback (official claim)
mwg:menu:5.story: Moving diagonally from "Export" down to "PDF" brushed over "Rename" and the submenu closed. The triangle sits on the path so siblings never get that hover.
mwg:menu:5.support: abs() and sign(): Baseline Newly available (since 2025-06-26)

mwg:menu:6.title: Move focus into the menu in the `toggle` event, not `command`
mwg:menu:6.action: On keyboard open, focus the first enabled item in the `toggle` listener; set `aria-expanded` only there too
mwg:menu:6.blocker: The `command` event fires before `toggle-popover` opens the menu, so focus can't move in yet (quote: "The `command` event fires before `toggle-popover` opens the menu, so focus cannot move into the menu there.")
mwg:menu:6.outcome: After a keyboard open, focus actually enters the menu (official claim)
mwg:menu:6.story: Enter opened the menu but focus stayed on the trigger, and Down did nothing.

mwg:menu:7.title: Close submenus one level at a time and restore focus to their trigger yourself
mwg:menu:7.action: Call `stopPropagation()` on Esc and ArrowLeft in submenus; focus the trigger before `hidePopover()`
mwg:menu:7.blocker: HTML restores focus only for the first `popover="auto"` in a stack, so nested levels must do it; without stopping propagation the parent's listener closes it too (quote: "HTML restores focus only for the first `popover="auto"` in a stack, so nested levels must restore focus to their trigger explicitly."; "or the parent's listener closes it too.")
mwg:menu:7.outcome: Esc closes only the submenu, focus returns to "Export" and the parent stays open (official claim)
mwg:menu:7.story: Esc in a submenu made the whole chain vanish and dropped focus somewhere on the page.

mwg:menu:8.title: Make the check-mark selector at least as specific as the base `::before` rule
mwg:menu:8.action: `[focusgroup~="menu"] button[aria-checked="true"]::before { content: "✓" }`, no less specific than the rule reserving the icon slot
mwg:menu:8.blocker: If it is less specific, the empty `content` wins and the check never shows (quote: "or the empty content wins and the check mark never shows.")
mwg:menu:8.outcome: Checked items show a check mark (official claim)
mwg:menu:8.story: "Show grid" was on, yet the menu showed no check.
mwg:menu:8.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:menu:9.title: Align menu rows with a fixed leading slot and `margin-inline-start: auto`, not subgrid
mwg:menu:9.action: Make items `display: flex` with a fixed-width `::before` for icon or check, and put shortcuts or submenu indicators in a `.hint` with `margin-inline-start: auto`
mwg:menu:9.blocker: With subgrid, any extra inline child (such as a badge) becomes its own grid item and breaks the layout (quote: "any extra inline child (a badge, for example) becomes its own grid item and breaks the layout.")
mwg:menu:9.outcome: Labels align with or without icons or an extra badge (official claim)
mwg:menu:9.story: Adding a "New" badge to one item misaligned every column in the menu.
mwg:menu:9.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:menu:10.title: Menu open animations need `@starting-style`
mwg:menu:10.action: Add `@starting-style { opacity: 0; translate: ... }` in the open state; include `display` and `overlay` in the transition with `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` on its own line
mwg:menu:10.blocker: A closed popover is `display: none` and transitions don't start from an unrendered state, so without start values the open snaps and only the close animates (quote: "Without it the open snaps and only the close animates.")
mwg:menu:10.outcome: Both open and close get short animations without delaying keyboard focus (official claim)
mwg:menu:10.story: The menu faded out when closing but popped in instantly when opening.
mwg:menu:10.support: @starting-style: no support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:navigation-drawer.title: Open and close the drawer with scroll snap and tie the backdrop dim to a scroll timeline
mwg:navigation-drawer.action: Inside a modal `<dialog>`, a horizontal scroller (one drawer-width column plus a full-viewport spacer) with `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory` rests only open or closed; `scroll-timeline` and `timeline-scope` bind `--drawer-backdrop` (registered as a number with `@property`) to the scroll position so `::backdrop` opacity follows; an IntersectionObserver calls `close()` only once the sheet has fully left
mwg:navigation-drawer.blocker: With JS-driven `transform` animations, the drawer's position is set by a tween, not the finger (quote: "the scroll mechanism gives the user direct control of the panel's position (their finger drives it, not a tween)")
mwg:navigation-drawer.outcome: The drawer moves exactly with the finger and the backdrop darkens in sync, with momentum and mid-gesture reversal handled by the browser; scroll snap is Widely available, scroll-driven animations Newly, with a `scroll` listener writing the dim where unsupported (official claim)
mwg:navigation-drawer.story: Pulling out a side menu on a phone used to play a fixed animation on release, and you couldn't pull it back halfway. As a scroller, the drawer is whatever is under your finger, and the backdrop dims with its position.
mwg:navigation-drawer.unlock: Finger-following drawers and bottom sheets used to need a gesture library → side navigation, bottom action sheets and pull-out filter panels can use native scrolling, darkening the backdrop as you drag and settling open or closed on release
mwg:navigation-drawer.support: Scroll snap: Widely. Scroll-driven animations: Baseline Newly available (since 2026-10-27). Registered custom properties: Newly

mwg:navigation-drawer:2.title: Don't use `closedby="any"` on a full-viewport drawer; detect taps outside the sheet yourself
mwg:navigation-drawer:2.action: Listen for `click` on the dialog and call the scroll-back `closeDrawer()` when the target isn't inside the sheet
mwg:navigation-drawer:2.blocker: The dialog fills the viewport, so taps land on the dialog rather than `::backdrop`, and it would close without the slide-out (quote: "the dialog fills the viewport, so taps land on the dialog rather than its ::backdrop, and it would close without the slide-out animation.")
mwg:navigation-drawer:2.outcome: Tapping the dimmed area slides the drawer out (official claim)
mwg:navigation-drawer:2.story: With `closedby="any"`, tapping the dim area made the drawer vanish instantly instead of sliding away.
mwg:navigation-drawer:2.support: <dialog closedby>: no support data in this guide; other guides record Limited

mwg:navigation-drawer:3.title: To close, scroll back first and only `close()` once the observer sees the sheet has left
mwg:navigation-drawer:3.action: `closeDrawer()` only scrolls to the spacer; the IntersectionObserver calls `drawer.close()` when visibility drops below the threshold; Esc's `cancel` is prevented and also slides out
mwg:navigation-drawer:3.blocker: Calling `close()` directly removes the element from the top layer mid-animation, hiding the close animation (quote: "doing so would remove the element from the top layer mid-animation and the close animation would not be visible.")
mwg:navigation-drawer:3.outcome: Swipe, button, backdrop tap and Esc all converge on one callback with the full close animation (official claim)
mwg:navigation-drawer:3.story: Pressing the close button made the drawer disappear rather than slide out.

mwg:navigation-drawer:4.title: Wrap the scroll-driven backdrop animation entirely in `@supports (animation-timeline: scroll())`
mwg:navigation-drawer:4.action: Put the `@keyframes`, `@property` and `animation-timeline` inside the `@supports` block
mwg:navigation-drawer:4.blocker: Unsupported browsers still parse the keyframes and apply the `0%` value, leaving the backdrop permanently dark (quote: "would apply the animation's `0%` value (--drawer-backdrop: 1) at all times, leaving the backdrop permanently opaque.")
mwg:navigation-drawer:4.outcome: Where unsupported, the JS fallback is the only writer of the dim (official claim)
mwg:navigation-drawer:4.story: In an older browser, after opening the drawer once, the background stayed dark after closing.

mwg:navigation-drawer:5.title: Register the backdrop custom property as a number with `@property`
mwg:navigation-drawer:5.blocker: Unregistered, the browser treats it as a string and can't interpolate, so the backdrop jumps from 0 to 1 (quote: "the backdrop would jump from 0 to 1 with no fade.")
mwg:navigation-drawer:5.outcome: The dim changes continuously while dragging (official claim)
mwg:navigation-drawer:5.story: Dragging the drawer didn't fade the background; it suddenly went black at some point.
mwg:navigation-drawer:5.support: Registered custom properties: Baseline Newly available (since 2024-07-09)

mwg:navigation-drawer:6.title: Size the drawer with `svh`, not `vh` or `dvh`
mwg:navigation-drawer:6.blocker: iOS Safari's address bar resizes mid-swipe, so `vh`/`dvh` make the sheet height jump (quote: "so the sheet height does not jump when the iOS Safari address bar resizes mid-swipe.")
mwg:navigation-drawer:6.outcome: Height stays fixed while swiping (official claim)
mwg:navigation-drawer:6.story: Pulling the drawer on an iPhone made its height twitch.
mwg:navigation-drawer:6.support: svh: no support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:navigation-drawer:7.title: A drawer that doubles as a sidebar uses `popover="manual"`, not `auto` or `hint`
mwg:navigation-drawer:7.action: Use a regular element with `role="dialog"` and `popover="manual"`, and handle inert, `aria-modal`, focus return and Esc yourself
mwg:navigation-drawer:7.blocker: The built-in light dismiss of `auto` and `hint` would fire mid-swipe (quote: "their built-in light-dismiss would also fire mid-swipe.")
mwg:navigation-drawer:7.outcome: Only your code decides when to close, so dragging never closes it by mistake (official claim)
mwg:navigation-drawer:7.story: Pushing the drawer back with a finger, it closed itself before the finger lifted.

mwg:navigation-drawer:8.title: Don't use `<dialog>` for a drawer that becomes a permanent sidebar on wide screens
mwg:navigation-drawer:8.action: When it doubles as a sidebar, use a regular element with `role="dialog"` and remove the role via `matchMedia()` in sidebar mode
mwg:navigation-drawer:8.blocker: `<dialog>` is always exposed as a dialog, but a sidebar isn't one (quote: "A `<dialog>` element does not work here, since it is always exposed as a dialog, but a sidebar is not one.")
mwg:navigation-drawer:8.outcome: It is ordinary navigation as a sidebar and a dialog as a drawer (official claim)
mwg:navigation-drawer:8.story: On desktop the fixed sidebar was announced as "dialog" every time.
mwg:navigation-drawer:8.support: No support data in the guide; N/A

mwg:navigation-drawer:9.title: Use `scroll-initial-target` so the drawer enters the top layer at its closed position, then slides in
mwg:navigation-drawer:9.action: Set `scroll-initial-target: nearest` on the spacer's `::after`, then `scrollTo({ left: 0 })` after `showModal()`; without support, jump to the closed position and wait two `requestAnimationFrame`s before scrolling back
mwg:navigation-drawer:9.blocker: Without an initial position the drawer appears already open with no slide-in, and with only one rAF the second `scrollTo` cancels the first (quote: "Without this, the drawer would appear instantly in the open position with no slide-in animation.")
mwg:navigation-drawer:9.outcome: Supporting browsers slide the drawer in from off-screen; Chrome/Edge 133 only, other browsers need the double-rAF script (official claim)
mwg:navigation-drawer:9.story: Tapping the menu button made the drawer simply appear instead of sliding out. An initial scroll position parks it off-screen first, so there is something to slide.
mwg:navigation-drawer:9.unlock: Scroll-based drawers used to need a scripted jump plus two frames of waiting → bottom sheets, side drawers and pull-out comment panels can start off-screen before entering and open with a single scroll. Chromium only for now
mwg:navigation-drawer:9.support: scroll-initial-target: Limited availability. Supported by: Chrome 133, Edge 133. Unsupported in: Firefox, Safari
